bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第183卷卷第一百八十三

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 183, juan 183.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 183.

sentences.zh: 【隋紀七】 起柔兆困敦，盡強圉赤備若五月，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Sui Records 7] Beginning Rouzhao Kundun, ending Qiangyu Chifenruo in the fifth month—in all, a little more than one year.
translations.idiomatic: [Sui Records 7] From Rouzhao Kundun through Qiangyu Chifenruo, fifth month—a span of a little more than one year.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，朝集使不至者二十餘郡，始議分遣使者十二道發兵討捕盜賊。

translations.literal: Spring, first month: more than twenty commanderies whose court-assembled envoys had not arrived—discussion began on dispatching envoys along twelve routes to raise troops to pursue and capture bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, envoys from more than twenty commanderies failed to appear at court, and the government first considered sending commissioners along twelve circuits to raise troops and hunt down the bandits.

sentences.zh: 詔毘陵通守路道德集十郡兵數萬人，於郡東南起宮苑，周圍十二里，內為十六離宮，大抵仿東都西苑之制，而奇麗過之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Piling circuit administrator Lu Daode to assemble troops from ten commanderies, numbering tens of thousands, and at the southeast of the commandery erect palace gardens twelve li in circumference, with sixteen detached palaces within—generally modeled on the Eastern Capital's Western Park but surpassing it in splendor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Lu Daode, defender of Piling, to gather tens of thousands of soldiers from ten commanderies and build a palace park southeast of the seat, twelve li around, containing sixteen detached palaces—roughly on the model of the Western Park at the eastern capital, but even more extravagant.

sentences.zh: 又欲築宮於會稽，會亂，不果成。

translations.literal: He also wished to build a palace at Kuaiji; rebellion broke out, and it was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: He also planned a palace at Kuaiji, but unrest intervened and the project was never finished.

sentences.zh: 三月，上巳，帝與群臣飲於西苑水上，命學士杜寶撰《水飾圖經》，采古水事七十二，使朝散大夫黃袞以木為之，間以妓航、酒船，人物自動如生，鐘磬箏瑟，能成音曲。

translations.literal: Third month, on the Shangsi festival, the emperor drank with his ministers on the waters of the Western Park, ordered academician Du Bao to compile the Water Ornament Canon, selecting seventy-two ancient water affairs, and had Gentleman for Court Discussion Huang Gun make them in wood, interspersed with pleasure boats and wine vessels—figures moving of themselves as if alive, bells, chimes, zithers, and lutes able to produce melodies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the Shangsi festival, the emperor feasted with his ministers on the Western Park's waters and ordered the scholar Du Bao to compile a Water Ornament Canon, gathering seventy-two tales of waters from antiquity. Huang Gun, Gentleman for Court Discussion, fashioned them in wood, mingling pleasure craft and wine boats among them; the figures moved by themselves as though alive, and bells, stone chimes, zithers, and lutes could actually play tunes.

sentences.zh: 己丑，張金稱陷平恩，一朝殺男女萬餘口；

translations.literal: On jichou, Zhang Jincheng took Ping'en and in a single morning killed more than ten thousand men and women;
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Zhang Jincheng captured Ping'en and in one morning slaughtered more than ten thousand men, women, and children;

sentences.zh: 又陷武安、鉅鹿、清河諸縣。

translations.literal: he also took the counties of Wu'an, Julu, and Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: then overran the counties of Wu'an, Julu, and Qinghe as well.

sentences.zh: 金稱比諸賊尤殘暴，所過民無孑遺。

translations.literal: Jincheng, compared with other bandits, was especially brutal; wherever he passed, not a single subject was left alive.
translations.idiomatic: Among the rebel leaders Jincheng was the most savage of all—wherever he marched, no commoner was left alive.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁巳，大業殿西院火。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on dingsi, fire broke out in the western courtyard of the Hall of Great Works.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on dingsi, fire destroyed the western wing of the Hall of Great Works.

sentences.zh: 帝以為盜起，驚走，入西苑，匿草間，火定乃還。

translations.literal: The emperor thought bandits had risen, fled in alarm, entered the Western Park, and hid among the grass; when the fire was out he returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took it for a rising of bandits, fled in panic into the Western Park, and hid in the undergrowth until the blaze died down.

sentences.zh: 帝自八年以後，每夜眠恆驚悸，雲有賊，令數婦人搖撫，乃得眠。

translations.literal: From the eighth year onward the emperor, whenever he slept at night, was constantly startled and fearful, saying there were bandits, and had several women rock and soothe him before he could sleep.
translations.idiomatic: After the eighth year of his reign he could scarcely sleep at night without waking in terror, crying that bandits were upon him; only when several women rocked and comforted him could he rest.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，歷山飛別將甄翟兒眾十萬寇太原，將軍潘長文敗死。

translations.literal: On guihai, Zhen Zhai'er, a detached general under Lishan Fei, with a host of a hundred thousand raided Taiyuan; General Pan Changwen was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Zhen Zhai'er—a lieutenant of the rebel Lishan Fei—led a hundred thousand men against Taiyuan; General Pan Changwen was defeated and slain.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙戌朔，日有食之，既。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on the first day bingxu, there was a solar eclipse, total.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the new moon of bingxu day, the sun was totally eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 壬午，帝於景華宮徵求螢火，得數斛，夜出遊山，放之，光遍巖谷。

translations.literal: On renwu, at Jinghua Palace the emperor gathered fireflies, obtaining several hu; at night he went touring the mountains, released them, and their light filled cliffs and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, at Jinghua Palace the emperor collected fireflies by the bushel; that night he roamed the hills and set them free until their glow filled every ravine and peak.

sentences.zh: 帝問侍臣盜賊，左翊衛大將軍宇文述曰：「漸少。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked his attendants about bandits; Left Wing Guard General Yuwen Shu said, "They are gradually fewer."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his attendants about the bandits, and Left Wing Guard General Yuwen Shu replied, "They are dwindling."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「比從來少幾何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Compared with before, by how much fewer?"
translations.idiomatic: "Compared with before," the emperor asked, "by how much have they fallen off?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「不能什一。」

translations.literal: He answered, "Not one in ten."
translations.idiomatic: "Not even a tenth," he answered."

sentences.zh: 納言蘇威引身隱柱，帝呼前問之，對曰：「臣非所司，不委多少，但患漸近。」

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Su Wei drew back and hid behind a pillar; the emperor called him forward and questioned him. He replied, "This subject's office is not concerned with the matter—I do not know the numbers, but I fear they are drawing gradually nearer."
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, Censor-in-Chief, had slipped behind a pillar; the emperor summoned him and asked the same question. Su Wei answered, "That is not my department—I cannot say how many there are—but I fear they are drawing ever closer."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何謂也？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What do you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: "What do you mean?" said the emperor."

sentences.zh: 威曰：「他日賊據長白山，今近在汜水。

translations.literal: Wei said, "In former days the bandits held Changbai Mountain; now they are close at Sishui.
translations.idiomatic: "Once they held Changbai Mountain," said Wei; "now they are at our gates in Sishui.

sentences.zh: 且往日租賦丁役，今皆何在！

translations.literal: Moreover, the men who once paid rent and taxes and performed corvée—where are they all now!
translations.idiomatic: And where are all the men who once paid taxes and bore corvée labor?

sentences.zh: 豈非其人皆化為盜乎！

translations.literal: Are they not all turned into bandits!
translations.idiomatic: Have they not every one become bandits themselves?

sentences.zh: 比見奏賊皆不以實，遂使失於支計，不時剪除。

translations.literal: Lately I see memorials on bandits that do not state the facts, so that planning goes awry and they are not cut down in time.
translations.idiomatic: The reports you receive understate the truth, so the court misjudges its resources and fails to strike them down in time.

sentences.zh: 又昔在雁門，許罷征遼，今復征發，賊何由息！」

translations.literal: Again, formerly at Wild Goose Gate you promised to halt the Liaodong campaign; now levies are renewed—how can the bandits be stilled!"
translations.idiomatic: And at Wild Goose Gate you promised to end the Liaodong war; now the levies are renewed—how can the rebels ever lay down their arms?"

sentences.zh: 帝不悅而罷。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and dismissed the session.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took offense and broke up the audience.

sentences.zh: 尋屬五月五日，百僚多饋珍玩，威獨獻《尚書》。

translations.literal: Soon it was the fifth day of the fifth month; the hundred officials mostly presented rare curios, but Wei alone presented the Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Before long came the fifth day of the fifth month, when the officials showered the throne with luxuries; Su Wei alone presented a copy of the Documents.

sentences.zh: 或譖之曰：「《尚書》有《五子之歌》，威意甚不遜。」

translations.literal: Someone slandered him, saying, "The Documents contains the 'Song of the Five Sons'—Wei's intent is very disrespectful."
translations.idiomatic: Someone whispered that the Documents contained the "Song of the Five Sons"—a barely veiled reproach—and that Wei's gesture was insolent in the extreme."

sentences.zh: 帝益怒。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angrier still.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's rage only deepened.

sentences.zh: 頃之，帝問威以伐高麗事，威欲帝知天下多盜，對曰：「今茲之役，願不發兵，但赦群盜，自可得數十萬。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor questioned Wei about attacking Goguryeo; Wei wished the emperor to know how many bandits there were in the realm and replied, "For this campaign, I wish you would not mobilize troops but only pardon the mass of bandits—you would yourself obtain several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the emperor asked Wei about the Goguryeo expedition. Wei, wanting him to grasp how many rebels roamed the land, said, "For this campaign, send no regular troops—merely pardon the bandit hosts, and you will have several hundred thousand men at once.

sentences.zh: 遣之東征，彼喜於免罪，爭務立功，高麗可滅。」

translations.literal: Send them east to campaign; they will rejoice at escaping punishment and vie to achieve merit—Goguryeo can be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch them eastward; grateful to be spared execution, they will fight for merit, and Goguryeo will fall."

sentences.zh: 帝不懌。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was not pleased.

sentences.zh: 威出，御史大夫裴蘊奏曰：「此大不遜！

translations.literal: When Wei had gone out, Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun memorialized, "This is grossly disrespectful!
translations.idiomatic: As Wei withdrew, Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun submitted: "This is rank insubordination!

sentences.zh: 天下何處有許多賊！」

translations.literal: Where in the realm are there so many bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: Where in the empire are there so many bandits?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「老革多奸，以賊脅我！

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The old hide is full of treachery—he threatens me with bandits!
translations.idiomatic: "The old rascal is full of guile," said the emperor; "he threatens me with bandits!

sentences.zh: 欲批其口，且復隱忍。」

translations.literal: I want to strike his mouth shut, yet for now I bear with it."
translations.idiomatic: I would strike his mouth shut, yet for the moment I hold my peace."

sentences.zh: 蘊知帝意，遣河南白衣張行本奏：「威昔在高陽典選，濫授人官；

translations.literal: Yun knew the emperor's mind and sent the commoner Zhang Xingben of Henan to memorialize: "Wei formerly at Gaoyang supervised selection and wantonly bestowed offices on men;
translations.idiomatic: Reading the emperor's mood, Yun had Zhang Xingben, a commoner of Henan, accuse Wei: "When he oversaw appointments at Gaoyang, he handed out offices recklessly;

sentences.zh: 畏怯突厥，請還京師。」

translations.literal: fearing the Turks, he asked to return to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: and, cowed by the Turks, begged to be sent back to the capital."

sentences.zh: 帝令按驗，獄成，下詔數威罪狀，除名為民。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered investigation and verification; when the case was complete, an edict enumerated Wei's crimes and struck his name from the rolls, making him a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an inquiry; when the case was proved, an edict listed Wei's offenses and struck him from office, reducing him to common status.

sentences.zh: 後月餘，復有奏威與突厥陰圖不軌者，事下裴蘊推之，蘊處威死。

translations.literal: A little more than a month later there was again a memorial that Wei and the Turks were secretly plotting sedition; the matter was sent down to Pei Yun to pursue, and Yun sentenced Wei to death.
translations.idiomatic: A month later came fresh charges that Wei had conspired with the Turks; the case went to Pei Yun, who recommended death.

sentences.zh: 威無以自明，但摧謝而已。

translations.literal: Wei had no means to clear himself and could only bow in broken submission.
translations.idiomatic: Wei could not clear himself and could only bow his head in submission.

sentences.zh: 帝憫而釋之，曰：「未忍即殺。」

translations.literal: The emperor pitied him and released him, saying, "I cannot yet bear to kill him at once."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity and spared him, saying, "I am not yet ready to kill him outright."

sentences.zh: 遂並其子孫三世皆除名。

translations.literal: Thereupon his sons and grandsons for three generations were all struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: But he struck Wei and three generations of his descendants from the registers.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬戌，濟景公樊子蓋卒。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on renxu, Duke Jing of Ji, Fan Zigai, died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renxu, Fan Zigai, Duke Jing of Ji, died.

sentences.zh: 江都新作龍舟成，送東都；

translations.literal: The newly built dragon boat at Jiangdu was completed and sent to the Eastern Capital;
translations.idiomatic: The new dragon boat built at Jiangdu was finished and sent to the eastern capital;

sentences.zh: 守文述勸幸江都，帝從之。

translations.literal: Yuwen Shu urged a journey to favor Jiangdu, and the emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu urged a progress to Jiangdu, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 右候衛大將軍酒泉趙才諫曰：「今百姓疲勞，府藏空竭，盜賊蜂起，禁令不行，願陛下還京師，安兆庶。」

translations.literal: Right Rear Guard General Zhao Cai of Jiuquan remonstrated: "Now the common people are exhausted, the treasury is empty, bandits swarm like bees, and prohibitions are not enforced—I wish Your Majesty would return to the capital and settle the myriad people."
translations.idiomatic: Right Rear Guard General Zhao Cai of Jiuquan remonstrated: "The people are worn out, the treasury is bare, bandits swarm everywhere, and your orders go unheeded. I beg Your Majesty to return to the capital and restore peace to the realm."

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，以才屬吏，旬日，意解，乃出之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and handed Cai over to the officials; after ten days his mood eased and he released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and handed Zhao Cai over to the law officers; ten days later his temper cooled and he set him free.

sentences.zh: 朝臣皆不欲行，帝意甚堅，無敢諫者。

translations.literal: The court ministers all did not wish to go, but the emperor's intent was very firm and none dared remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: The courtiers were united in wishing to stay, but the emperor's mind was made up and no one dared speak against the journey.

sentences.zh: 建節尉任宗上書極諫，即日於朝堂杖殺之。

translations.literal: Establishment Commandant Ren Zong submitted a memorial of fierce remonstrance and was beaten to death that same day in the audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: Establishment Commandant Ren Zong submitted a fierce memorial of protest and was clubbed to death in the audience hall that very day.

sentences.zh: 甲子，帝幸江都，命越王侗與光祿大夫段達、太府卿元文都、檢校民部尚書韋津、右武衛將軍皇甫天逸、右司郎盧楚等總留後事。

translations.literal: On jiazi the emperor proceeded to Jiangdu, ordering Prince of Yue Yang Tong together with Household Grandee Duan Da, Grand Steward of the Palace Yuan Wendu, acting Minister of Revenue Wei Jin, Right Martial Guard General Huangfu Tianyi, Right Secretariat Gentleman Lu Chu, and others to oversee all affairs left behind.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the emperor set out for Jiangdu, leaving Prince of Yue Yang Tong with Household Grandee Duan Da, Palace Grand Steward Yuan Wendu, acting Minister of Revenue Wei Jin, Right Martial Guard General Huangfu Tianyi, Right Secretariat Gentleman Lu Chu, and others to govern the capital in his absence.

sentences.zh: 津，孝寬之子也。

translations.literal: Jin was the son of Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jin was a son of the great general Wei Xiaokuan.

sentences.zh: 帝以詩留別宮人曰：「我夢江都好，征遼亦偶然。」

translations.literal: The emperor left a parting poem for the palace women, saying, "I dreamed Jiangdu was fine; the Liaodong campaign too was mere chance."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left a parting verse for the palace women: "I dreamed Jiangdu fair; the Liaodong war was chance alone."

sentences.zh: 奉信郎崔民象以盜賊充斥，於建國門上表諫；

translations.literal: Gentleman for Attendance Cui Minxiang, because bandits filled the land, submitted a remonstrance at the Gate of Establishing the Realm;
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman for Attendance Cui Minxiang, citing the bandits that filled the land, submitted a memorial of protest at the Gate of Establishing the Realm;

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，先解其頤，然後斬之。

translations.literal: the emperor was greatly angered, first had his jaw unhinged, then beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor was furious, had his jaw torn loose, and then beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，馮翊孫華舉兵為盜。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Sun Hua of Fengyi raised troops and became a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Sun Hua of Fengyi took up arms as a rebel leader.

sentences.zh: 虞世基以盜賊充斥，請發兵屯洛口倉，帝曰：「卿是書生，定猶恇怯。」

translations.literal: Yu Shiji, because bandits filled the land, requested troops be sent to garrison Luokou Granary; the emperor said, "You are a bookish man—surely still timid and fearful."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shiji, alarmed at the bandits everywhere, asked that troops garrison Luokou Granary; the emperor said, "You are a scholar—no doubt still timid."

sentences.zh: 戊辰，車駕至鞏。

translations.literal: On wuchen the imperial carriage reached Gong.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the imperial train reached Gong.

sentences.zh: 敕有司移箕山、公路二府於倉內，仍令築城以備不虞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the authorities to move the two prefectures of Jishan and Gonglu inside the granary and also to build a wall against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Jishan and Gonglu prefectural offices moved inside the granary compound and commanded that a defensive wall be thrown up against surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 至汜水，奉信郎王愛仁復上表請還西京，帝斬之而行。

translations.literal: When they reached Sishui, Gentleman for Attendance Wang Airen again submitted a memorial asking to return to the Western Capital; the emperor beheaded him and went on.
translations.idiomatic: At Sishui, Gentleman for Attendance Wang Airen again begged the court to turn back to the western capital; the emperor had him executed and pressed on.

sentences.zh: 至梁郡，郡人邀車駕上書曰：「陛下若遂幸江都，天下非陛下之有！」

translations.literal: At Liang commandery, men of the commandery intercepted the imperial carriage and submitted a memorial: "If Your Majesty insists on proceeding to Jiangdu, the realm will no longer be Your Majesty's!"
translations.idiomatic: At Liang commandery the local people waylaid the imperial procession with a petition: "If Your Majesty persists in going to Jiangdu, the empire will slip from your grasp!"

sentences.zh: 又斬之。

translations.literal: He beheaded them again.
translations.idiomatic: He had them executed as well.

sentences.zh: 是時李子通據海陵，左才相掠淮北，杜伏威屯六合，眾各數萬；

translations.literal: At this time Li Zitong held Hailing, Zuo Caixiang plundered north of the Huai, Du Fuwei encamped at Liuhe—each host numbered tens of thousands;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Zitong held Hailing, Zuo Caixiang ravaged north of the Huai, and Du Fuwei camped at Liuhe—each commanded tens of thousands of men;

sentences.zh: 帝遣光祿大夫陳稜將宿衛精兵八千討之，往往克捷。

translations.literal: the emperor sent Household Grandee Chen Leng to lead eight thousand picked palace-guard troops against them, and he often won victories.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor sent Household Grandee Chen Leng with eight thousand elite palace guards against them, and Chen won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙巳，賊帥趙萬海眾數十萬，自恆山寇高陽。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on yisi, bandit chief Zhao Wanhai with a host of several hundred thousand from Hengshan raided Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yisi, the rebel chief Zhao Wanhai led several hundred thousand men from Hengshan against Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己丑，許恭公宇文述卒。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on jichou, Duke Gong of Xu, Yuwen Shu, died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jichou, Yuwen Shu, Duke Gong of Xu, died.

sentences.zh: 初，述子化及、智及皆無賴。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shu's sons Huaji and Zhiji were both wastrels.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu's sons Huaji and Zhiji had long been wastrels.

sentences.zh: 化及事帝於東宮，帝寵暱之，及即位，以為太僕少卿。

translations.literal: Huaji attended the emperor in the Eastern Palace; the emperor favored and was close to him, and when he took the throne he made him Vice Director of the Palace Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji had served the emperor when he was heir apparent and won his affection; on his accession the emperor made him Vice Director of the Palace Stud.

sentences.zh: 帝幸榆林，化及、智及冒禁與突厥交市，帝怒，將斬之，已解衣辮發，既而釋之，賜述為奴。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Yulin, Huaji and Zhiji violated the ban and traded with the Turks; the emperor was angry and was about to behead them—they had already loosened their clothes and unbraided their hair—then released them and bestowed them on Shu as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's visit to Yulin, Huaji and Zhiji defied the prohibition and traded with the Turks. The emperor flew into a rage and was about to execute them—they had already stripped and unbound their hair—then relented and gave them to their father as slaves.

sentences.zh: 智及弟士及，以尚主之故，常輕智及，唯化及與之親暱。

translations.literal: Zhiji's younger brother Shiji, because he had married an imperial princess, often looked down on Zhiji; only Huaji was close and intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiji's younger brother Shiji, having married an imperial princess, often looked down on Zhiji; only Huaji remained close to him.

sentences.zh: 述卒，帝復以化及為右屯衛將軍，智及為將作少監。

translations.literal: When Shu died, the emperor again made Huaji Right Rear Guard General and Zhiji Vice Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu's death the emperor restored Huaji as Right Rear Guard General and Zhiji as Vice Director of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 李密之亡也，往依郝孝德，孝德不禮之；

translations.literal: When Li Mi was in flight he went to rely on Hao Xiaode, but Xiaode did not treat him with courtesy;
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi was on the run he sought refuge with Hao Xiaode, who treated him coldly;

sentences.zh: 又入王薄，薄亦不之奇也。

translations.literal: he also entered Wang Bo's band, but Bo too did not regard him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: he then joined Wang Bo's band, but Bo likewise saw nothing remarkable in him.

sentences.zh: 密困乏，至削樹皮而食之，匿於淮陽村舍，變姓名，聚徒教授。

translations.literal: Mi was destitute, even peeling tree bark to eat; he hid in a village house in Huaiyang, changed his name, gathered disciples, and taught.
translations.idiomatic: Reduced to peeling bark from trees for food, he hid in a Huaiyang farmhouse under an assumed name, gathering pupils and teaching school.

sentences.zh: 郡縣疑而捕之，密亡去，抵其妹夫雍丘令丘君明。

translations.literal: The commandery and county suspected him and arrested him; Mi fled and reached his brother-in-law Qiu Junming, magistrate of Yongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: The local authorities grew suspicious and moved to seize him; Mi escaped and made his way to his brother-in-law Qiu Junming, magistrate of Yongqiu.

sentences.zh: 君明不敢捨，轉寄密於遊俠王秀才家，秀才以女妻之。

translations.literal: Junming dared not harbor him and instead lodged Mi with the wandering knight Wang Xiucai's household; the xiucai gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Junming dared not shelter him openly and passed him to the swordsman Wang Xiucai, who gave Mi his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 君明從侄懷義告其事，帝令懷義自繼敕書與梁郡通守楊汪相知收捕。

translations.literal: Junming's nephew by marriage Huaiyi reported the affair; the emperor ordered Huaiyi himself to carry the sealed edict and coordinate with Yang Wang, defender of Liang commandery, to seize and capture him.
translations.idiomatic: Junming's nephew Huaiyi informed on them; the emperor had Huaiyi carry the sealed warrant himself and coordinate with Yang Wang, defender of Liang commandery, to take Mi.

sentences.zh: 汪遣兵圍秀才宅，適值密出外，由是獲免，君明、秀才皆死。

translations.literal: Wang sent troops to surround the xiucai's house; it happened that Mi was out, and so he escaped; Junming and the xiucai both died.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wang sent soldiers to surround Wang Xiucai's house; Mi happened to be away and so survived, but Junming and Wang Xiucai were both put to death.

sentences.zh: 韋城翟讓為東都法曹，坐事當斬。

translations.literal: Zhai Rang of Weicheng served as law officer of the Eastern Capital and, implicated in a case, was to be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang of Weicheng had served as a legal officer at the eastern capital and, implicated in a crime, was condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 獄吏黃君漢奇其驍勇，夜中潛謂讓曰：「翟法司，天時人事，抑亦可知，豈能守死獄中乎！」

translations.literal: The prison officer Huang Junhan marveled at his valor; in the night he secretly said to Rang, "Law Officer Zhai, the signs of heaven and the affairs of men can perhaps be known—how can you keep death in prison!"
translations.idiomatic: The jailer Huang Junhan admired his courage and spirit. In the dead of night he whispered to him, "Law Officer Zhai, the times and the heavens speak plainly enough—will you simply die in this cell?"

sentences.zh: 讓驚喜叩頭曰：「讓，圈牢之豕，死生唯黃曹主所命！」

translations.literal: Rang, startled and delighted, kowtowed and said, "Rang is a pig in the pen—the living and the dead are at Master Huang's command alone!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang, astonished and grateful, kowtowed and said, "I am but a pig in the sty—my life or death rests entirely with you, Master Huang!"

sentences.zh: 君漢即破械出之。

translations.literal: Junhan at once broke his fetters and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Junhan broke his chains and set him free on the spot.

sentences.zh: 讓再拜曰：「讓蒙再生之恩則幸矣，奈黃曹主何！」

translations.literal: Rang bowed again and said, "If Rang receives the grace of rebirth I am fortunate—but what of Master Huang!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang bowed again. "If I live, it is your gift—but what will become of you, Master Huang?"

sentences.zh: 因泣下。

translations.literal: and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He burst into tears.

sentences.zh: 君漢怒曰：「本以公為大丈夫，可救生民之命，故不顧其死以奉脫，奈何反效兒女子涕泣相謝乎！

translations.literal: Junhan angrily said, "I took you for a great man who could save the lives of the people, and therefore did not regard my own death in setting you free—why do you instead imitate women and children, weeping and thanking each other!
translations.idiomatic: Huang Junhan snapped, "I thought you a man who might save the people, and risked my life to free you—why do you weep and thank me like some fretful woman?

sentences.zh: 君但努力自免，勿憂吾也！」

translations.literal: You need only strive to save yourself—do not worry for me!"
translations.idiomatic: Save yourself if you can, and spare no thought for me!"

sentences.zh: 讓遂亡命於瓦崗為群盜，同郡單雄信，驍健，善用馬槊，聚少年往從之。

translations.literal: Rang then fled for his life to Wagang as leader of a band of robbers; Shan Xiongxin of the same commandery, bold and strong, skilled with the cavalry lance, gathered youths and went to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang fled to Wagang and became a bandit chief. Shan Xiongxin of the same commandery—a fierce fighter skilled with the cavalry lance—rallied young men and joined him.

sentences.zh: 離狐徐世勣家於衛南，年十七，有勇略，說讓曰：「東郡於公與勣皆為鄉里，人多相識，不宜侵掠。

translations.literal: Xu Shiji of Lihu, whose family lived south of Wei, at seventeen years had courage and strategy; he said to Rang, "In Dong commandery both you and Shiji are from the same countryside—many people know each other; it is not fitting to plunder there.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shiji of Lihu, whose family lived south of Wei, was seventeen and already bold and resourceful. He urged Zhai Rang, "In Dong commandery we are all neighbors—too many would recognize us. We should not raid there.

sentences.zh: 滎陽、梁郡，汴水所經，剽行舟、掠商旅，足以自資。」

translations.literal: Xingyang and Liang commandery lie along the Bian River—seizing passing boats and plundering merchants and travelers is enough to support ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: But Xingyang and Liang commandery lie on the Bian Canal—seizing river craft and robbing merchants will keep us supplied."

sentences.zh: 讓然之，引眾入二郡界，掠公私船，資用豐給，附者益眾，聚徒至萬餘人。

translations.literal: Rang approved, led his host into the borders of the two commanderies, plundered public and private vessels, and had abundant supplies; those who joined grew ever more numerous, and his followers gathered to more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang agreed, led his men into both commanderies, and preyed on public and private shipping until his stores overflowed. Followers flocked to him until his band numbered more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 時又有外黃王當仁、濟陽王伯當、韋城周文舉、雍丘李公逸等皆擁眾為盜。

translations.literal: At this time there were also Wang Dangren of Waihuang, Wang Bodang of Jiyang, Zhou Wenju of Weicheng, Li Gongyi of Yongqiu, and others—all holding hosts and becoming bandits.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time Wang Dangren of Waihuang, Wang Bodang of Jiyang, Zhou Wenju of Weicheng, Li Gongyi of Yongqiu, and others each raised bands of their own.

sentences.zh: 李密自雍州亡命，往來諸帥間，說以取天下之策，始皆不信。

translations.literal: Li Mi, a fugitive from Yong province, went among the various chiefs and spoke to them of strategies to take the realm; at first none believed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi, fugitive from the capital region, moved among these chiefs preaching strategies to seize the empire; at first none believed him.

sentences.zh: 久之，稍以為然，相謂曰：「斯人公卿子弟，志氣若是。

translations.literal: After a long while they gradually came to think it so and said to one another, "This man is a son of the high nobility, and his spirit is like this.
translations.idiomatic: In time they began to listen, saying among themselves, "Here is a scion of the great houses, and his spirit is unmistakable.

sentences.zh: 今人人皆雲楊氏將滅，李氏將興。

translations.literal: Now everyone says the Yang house will perish and the Li house will rise.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone now says the Yang will fall and the Li will rise.

sentences.zh: 吾聞王者不死。

translations.literal: I have heard that one destined for kingship does not die.
translations.idiomatic: They say a man marked for kingship cannot be killed.

sentences.zh: 斯人再三獲濟，豈非其人乎！」

translations.literal: This man has again and again escaped death—is he not the one!"
translations.idiomatic: This man has slipped the noose again and again—is he not the one?"

sentences.zh: 由是漸敬密。

translations.literal: From this they gradually respected Mi.
translations.idiomatic: From that day they treated Li Mi with growing respect.

sentences.zh: 密察諸帥唯翟讓最強，乃因王伯當以見讓，為讓畫策，往說諸小盜，皆下之。

translations.literal: Mi observed that among the chiefs only Zhai Rang was strongest; through Wang Bodang he was introduced to Rang, drew up plans for him, went to persuade the lesser bandits, and all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi saw that Zhai Rang was the strongest of the chiefs; through Wang Bodang he gained an audience, laid out a plan, and went among the smaller bands until all submitted to Rang.

sentences.zh: 讓悅，稍親近密，與之計事，密因說讓曰：「劉、項皆起布衣為帝王。

translations.literal: Rang was pleased, drew gradually closer to Mi, and deliberated affairs with him; Mi thereupon said to Rang, "Liu and Xiang both rose from common cloth to become emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang was delighted, drew Li Mi into his counsels, and Li Mi told him, "Liu Bang and Xiang Yu both rose from commoners to rule as emperors.

sentences.zh: 今主昏於上，民怨於下，銳兵盡於遼東，和親絕於突厥，方乃巡遊揚、越，委棄東都，此亦劉、項奮起之會也。

translations.literal: Now the ruler above is benighted and the people below resent; sharp troops are exhausted in Liaodong, peace marriage is severed with the Turks, and he is just then touring Yang and Yue and abandoning the Eastern Capital—this too is the moment for Liu and Xiang to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Today the ruler is blind above and the people seethe below; his best troops are spent in Liaodong, his peace with the Turks is broken, and he wanders off to Yang and Yue while leaving the eastern capital undefended. This is the very hour in which Liu and Xiang seized their chance.

sentences.zh: 以足下雄才大略，士馬精銳，席捲二京，誅滅暴虐，隋氏不足亡也！」

translations.literal: With your heroic talent and grand design, your soldiers and horses sharp and elite, sweeping through the two capitals and destroying the tyrannical and cruel—the House of Sui is scarcely too much for you to overthrow!
translations.idiomatic: With talent like yours and troops like these, you could sweep both capitals, cut down the tyrants, and bring the House of Sui to its end without breaking stride."

sentences.zh: 讓謝曰：「吾儕群盜，旦夕偷生草間，君之言者，非吾所及也。」

translations.literal: Rang declined and said: "We are a band of robbers together, stealing our lives day and night in the grass and weeds; what you say is beyond what I can reach."
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang demurred. "We are nothing but outlaws scrabbling for life in the weeds. What you describe is far beyond men like us."

sentences.zh: 會有李玄英者，自東都逃來，經歷諸賊，求訪李密，云「斯人當代隋家」。

translations.literal: There happened to be one Li Xuanying, who fled from the Eastern Capital, passed through various bandit groups seeking Li Mi, and said, "This man is destined to replace the House of Sui."
translations.idiomatic: About this time a man named Li Xuanying fled the Eastern Capital, wandered through one rebel camp after another in search of Li Mi, and declared, "This is the man destined to replace the House of Sui."

sentences.zh: 人問其故，玄英言：「比來民間謠歌有《桃李章》曰：『桃李子，皇后繞揚州，宛轉花園裡。

translations.literal: When people asked the reason, Xuanying said: "Recently among the people there is a ballad called 'The Peach and Plum Charms,' which says: 'Peach and plum child, the empress circles Yangzhou, winding through the garden.
translations.idiomatic: Asked to explain, Xuanying said a folk song called "Peach and Plum" had lately been circulating: "Peach-and-plum boy, the empress roams Yangzhou, turning and turning in the garden.

sentences.zh: 勿浪語，誰道許！』

translations.literal: Do not speak rashly—who would dare say so!'
translations.idiomatic: Do not speak lightly—who would dare say such a thing!"

sentences.zh: 『桃李子』，謂逃亡者李氏之子也；

translations.literal: Peach and plum child' refers to a son of the Li clan, one of the fugitives;
translations.idiomatic: Peach-and-plum boy" points to a fugitive son of the Li clan;

sentences.zh: 皇與後，皆君也；

translations.literal: 'emperor' and 'empress' both mean 'lord';
translations.idiomatic: The words "emperor" and "empress" both signify "sovereign";

sentences.zh: 『宛轉花園裡』，謂天子在揚州無還日，將轉於溝壑也；

translations.literal: 'Winding through the garden' means the Son of Heaven at Yangzhou will have no day of return, but will turn into ditch and gully;
translations.idiomatic: "Turning and turning in the garden" means the emperor at Yangzhou will never come home again, but will end in a ditch;

sentences.zh: 『莫浪語，誰道許』者，密也。」

translations.literal: Do not speak rashly, who would dare say so'—that is Mi."
translations.idiomatic: Do not speak lightly—who would dare say such a thing?" That word is Mi."

sentences.zh: 既與密遇，遂委身事之。

translations.literal: Having met Mi, he thereupon devoted himself to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he found Li Mi, he pledged himself to his service.

sentences.zh: 前宋城尉齊郡房彥藻，自負其才，恨不為時用，預於楊玄感之謀。

translations.literal: The former Songcheng district captain Fang Yanzao of Qi Commandery, confident in his own talent and resentful that he had no employment in the age, had taken part in Yang Xuangan's plot.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yanzao of Qi, once captain of Songcheng district, thought highly of his own abilities and bitterly resented his wasted years; he had joined Yang Xuangan's conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 變姓名亡命，遇密於梁、宋之間，遂與之俱游漢、沔，遍入諸賊，說其豪傑；

translations.literal: He changed his name and fled for his life; meeting Mi between Liang and Song, he then traveled with him through Han and Mian, entering every bandit group to persuade their champions;
translations.idiomatic: He changed his name and went into hiding. He met Li Mi in the borderlands of Liang and Song, and together they traveled the Han and Mian regions, passing through rebel bands one by one to win over their leaders.

sentences.zh: 還日，從者數百人，仍為遊客，處於讓營。

translations.literal: On his return, several hundred followed him; still posing as a traveler, he lodged in Rang's camp.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, several hundred men followed in his train. Still passing as an itinerant guest, he took up residence in Zhai Rang's camp.

sentences.zh: 讓見密為豪傑所歸，欲從其計，猶豫未決。

translations.literal: "Rang saw that the champions were rallying to Mi, wished to adopt his plans, but hesitated and could not decide."
translations.idiomatic: "Zhai Rang saw the best men gathering around Li Mi and wanted to follow his counsel, yet he wavered, unable to decide."

sentences.zh: 有賈雄者，曉陰陽占候，為讓軍師，言無不用。

translations.literal: There was one Jia Xiong, skilled in yin-yang divination and astronomical omens, who served as Rang's military adviser—none of his words went unused.
translations.idiomatic: Among them was Jia Xiong, versed in yin-yang lore and divination, who served as Zhai Rang's strategist. Rang never ignored his advice.

sentences.zh: 密深結於雄，使之托術數以說讓；

translations.literal: Mi bonded deeply with Xiong and had him use occult arts to persuade Rang;
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi cultivated Jia Xiong closely and set him to persuade Zhai Rang under the guise of divination;

sentences.zh: 雄許諾，懷之未發。

translations.literal: Xiong agreed, but kept it in his heart and did not yet speak.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong agreed, but held the matter in his breast and did not yet reveal it.

sentences.zh: 會讓召雄，告以密所言，問其可否，對曰：「吉不可言。」

translations.literal: When Rang happened to summon Xiong, told him what Mi had said, and asked whether it was feasible, he replied: "The auspice cannot be put into words."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhai Rang summoned Xiong, repeated Li Mi's proposal, and asked whether it would succeed. Xiong answered, "The omen is too auspicious to speak of."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「公自立恐未必成，若立斯人，事無不濟。」

translations.literal: He also said: "If you raise yourself up, success may not be assured; but if you raise this man, nothing will fail."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "If you proclaim yourself leader, success is uncertain. Raise this man instead, and nothing you attempt will fail."

sentences.zh: 讓曰：「如卿言，蒲山公當自立，何來從我？」

translations.literal: Rang said: "According to your words, the Duke of Pushan ought to set himself up—why would he come to follow me?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang said, "By your reasoning the Duke of Pushan should rule in his own name. Why would he come and serve under me?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「事有相因。

translations.literal: He replied: "Affairs have their mutual dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong replied, "All things depend on one another.

sentences.zh: 所以來者，將軍姓翟，翟者，澤也，蒲非澤不生，故須將軍也。」

translations.literal: The reason he has come is that the General's surname is Zhai; Zhai means marsh—rush cannot grow except in marshes, hence the General is needed."
translations.idiomatic: He comes to you because your surname is Zhai—'marsh.' Rushes do not flourish except in marshland. He needs you, General, to thrive."

sentences.zh: 讓然之，與密情好日篤。

translations.literal: Rang assented to this; his friendship with Mi grew daily closer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang accepted this reasoning, and his bond with Li Mi grew warmer by the day.

sentences.zh: 密因說讓曰：「今四海糜沸，不得耕耘，公士眾雖多，食無倉稟，唯資野掠，常苦不給。

translations.literal: Mi thereupon said to Rang: "Now the four seas seethe like porridge—nothing can be cultivated. Though your troops are many, you have no granary stores; you rely solely on raiding in the wilds and constantly suffer want.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi pressed Zhai Rang: "The realm is in turmoil and the fields lie untilled. Your force is large, but you have no granaries—only what you seize on raids, and even that never lasts.

sentences.zh: 若曠日持久，加以大敵臨之，必渙然離散。

translations.literal: If this drags on day after day, and a great enemy presses upon you, you will surely dissolve and scatter.
translations.idiomatic: If this goes on, and a powerful foe closes in, your army will break apart like water.

sentences.zh: 未若先取滎陽，休兵館谷，待士馬肥充，然後與人爭利。」

translations.literal: It would be better to take Xingyang first, rest the troops and store grain, wait until men and horses are fat and full, and then vie with others for advantage."
translations.idiomatic: Better to seize Xingyang first, let the men rest and fill the stores, fatten horses and soldiers, and only then contend for mastery."

sentences.zh: 讓從之，於是破金堤關，攻滎陽諸縣，多下之。

translations.literal: Rang followed this counsel; they broke through Jindi Pass, attacked the counties of Xingyang, and captured most of them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang agreed. They stormed Jindi Pass, overran the counties around Xingyang, and took most of them.

sentences.zh: 滎陽太守郇王慶，弘之子也，不能討，帝徙張須阤為滎陽通守以討之。

translations.literal: Xingyang's prefect Xun Wang Qing, son of Hong, could not suppress them; the Emperor moved Zhang Xueta to be Xingyang's general defender to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Xingyang, Xun Wang Qing—son of Wang Hong—could not put them down. The emperor replaced him with Zhang Xueta as general defender of Xingyang and ordered him to destroy the rebels.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，須阤引兵擊讓，讓向數為須阤所敗，聞其來，大懼，將避之。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Xueta led troops to attack Rang; Rang had been defeated by Xueta several times before, and on hearing of his approach was greatly afraid and prepared to flee.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengxu, Zhang Xueta marched against Zhai Rang. Rang had already lost to him more than once; when he heard Xueta was coming, he was terrified and meant to run.

sentences.zh: 密曰：「須阤勇而無謀，兵又驟勝，既驕且狠，可一戰擒也。

translations.literal: Mi said: "Xueta is brave but without stratagem; his troops have suddenly won and are both arrogant and fierce—we can capture him in a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi said, "Xueta is brave but no strategist. His men have won too quickly—they are proud and brutal. One battle is enough to take him.

sentences.zh: 公但列陳以待，密保為公破之。」

translations.literal: Your lordship need only deploy in battle order and wait—I guarantee I will break him for you."
translations.idiomatic: Deploy your line and hold your ground. I will break him for you."

sentences.zh: 讓不得已，勒兵將戰，密分兵千餘人伏於大海寺北林間。

translations.literal: Rang had no choice; he marshaled his troops to give battle. Mi detached over a thousand men and hid them in the woods north of Dahai Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang, with no alternative, drew up his army to fight. Li Mi sent more than a thousand men into ambush in the forest north of Dahai Temple.

sentences.zh: 須阤素輕讓，方陳而前，讓與戰，不利，須阤乘之，逐北十餘里；

translations.literal: Xueta had always looked down on Rang; just as his battle line was advancing, he fought Rang to disadvantage; Xueta pressed the advantage and pursued north for more than ten li;
translations.idiomatic: Xueta had always despised Zhai Rang. As his line moved forward, Rang gave ground; Xueta pressed the attack and chased the fleeing rebels more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 密發伏掩之，須阤兵敗。

translations.literal: Mi launched the ambush and struck him; Xueta's army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi sprang the ambush. Xueta's army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 密與讓及徐世勣、王伯當合軍圍之，須阤潰圍出；

translations.literal: Mi joined with Rang, Xu Shiji, and Wang Bodang to combine forces and surround him; Xueta burst through the encirclement;
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi, Zhai Rang, Xu Shiji, and Wang Bodang united their forces and closed the ring. Xueta broke out of the encirclement,

sentences.zh: 左右不能盡出，須阤躍馬復入救之，來往數四，遂戰死。

translations.literal: not all his attendants could get out; Xueta leaped his horse back in to rescue them, going back and forth four times, and finally died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: but not all his men could follow. Four times he wheeled his horse back into the press to save them, and at last fell fighting.

sentences.zh: 所部兵晝夜號哭，數日不止，河南郡縣為之喪氣。

translations.literal: His troops wailed day and night without cease for many days; the commanderies and counties of Henan lost heart on his account.
translations.idiomatic: His soldiers wept day and night for days on end, and every garrison in Henan lost its nerve.

sentences.zh: 鷹揚郎將河東賈務本為須阤之副，亦被傷，帥餘眾五千餘人奔梁郡，務本尋卒。

translations.literal: Yingyang Lang General Jia Wuben of Hedong, Xueta's deputy, was also wounded; he led the remaining five thousand-odd men in flight to Liang Commandery, and Wuben soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Wuben of Hedong, Yingyang Lang General and Xueta's second-in-command, was wounded as well. He fled with some five thousand survivors to Liang Commandery and died soon after.

sentences.zh: 詔以光祿大夫裴仁基為河南道討捕大使，代領其眾，徙鎮虎牢。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Grandee of Splendid Happiness Pei Renji as Henan Circuit commissioner for suppression and arrest, to take command of Xueta's forces in his stead, and transferred his garrison to Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Pei Renji, Grandee of Splendid Happiness, commissioner for the suppression of bandits in Henan, to take over Xueta's command and garrison the force at Hulao.

sentences.zh: 讓乃令密建牙，別統所部，號薄山公營。

translations.literal: Rang then had Mi raise a headquarters banner and command his own division separately, called the Duke of Pushan Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang then allowed Li Mi to raise his own standard and command a separate division, known as the Duke of Pushan Camp.

sentences.zh: 密部分嚴整，凡號令士卒，雖盛夏，皆如背負霜雪。

translations.literal: Mi's division was sternly ordered; whenever he issued commands to the soldiers, even in midsummer they felt as if frost and snow weighed on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi's camp was run with iron discipline. Even in the heat of midsummer, his orders fell on the men like winter frost on their backs.

sentences.zh: 躬服儉素，所得金寶，悉頒賜麾下，由是人為之用。

translations.literal: He personally dressed plainly and simply; all gold and treasure obtained he distributed entirely among his subordinates, wherefore men gave themselves to his use.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly himself and gave every scrap of gold and booty to his officers and men. For that reason they served him willingly.

sentences.zh: 麾下士卒多為讓士卒所陵辱，以威約有素，不敢報也。

translations.literal: Many of his subordinate soldiers were insulted and abused by Rang's soldiers; because his authority and discipline had long been established, they dared not retaliate.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Li Mi's soldiers were bullied and humiliated by Zhai Rang's men, but Li Mi's stern rule was well established, and they did not dare strike back.

sentences.zh: 讓謂密曰：「今資糧粗足，意欲還向瓦崗，公若不往，唯公所適，讓從此別矣。」

translations.literal: Rang said to Mi: "Now our provisions are roughly sufficient; I intend to return toward Wagang. If you will not go, go wherever you please—Rang will part from here."
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang told Li Mi, "We have enough supplies for now, and I mean to return to Wagang. If you won't come, go where you will—I part from you here."

sentences.zh: 讓帥輜重東引，密亦西行至康城，說下數城，大獲資儲。

translations.literal: Rang led the baggage train eastward; Mi also went west to Kangcheng, persuaded several cities to submit, and gained great stores.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang marched east with the baggage train. Li Mi went west to Kangcheng, brought several towns over by persuasion, and amassed great stores of grain and supplies.

sentences.zh: 讓尋悔，復引兵從密。

translations.literal: Before long Rang repented and again led troops to follow Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhai Rang regretted his decision and marched after Li Mi with his army.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽賊帥操師乞自稱元興王，建元始興，攻陷豫章郡，以其鄉人林士弘為大將軍。

translations.literal: Poyang bandit chief Cao Shiji proclaimed himself King of Yuanxing, set the era name Yuanshi, captured Yuzhang Commandery, and appointed his fellow townsman Lin Shihong as Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shiji, leader of the Poyang rebels, declared himself King of Yuanxing, adopted the era name Beginning of Yuanshi, seized Yuzhang Commandery, and made his townsman Lin Shihong grand general.

sentences.zh: 詔治書侍御史劉子翊將兵討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Investigative Censor Liu Ziyi to lead troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Liu Ziyi, investigative censor, to take an army against him.

sentences.zh: 師乞中流矢死，士弘代統其眾，與子翊戰於彭蠡湖，子翊敗死。

translations.literal: Shiji was struck by a stray arrow and died; Shihong took command of his forces in his stead, fought Ziyi at Lake Poyang, and Ziyi was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shiji took an arrow and died. Lin Shihong assumed command, met Liu Ziyi on Lake Poyang, and killed him in defeat.

sentences.zh: 士弘兵大振，至十餘萬人。

translations.literal: Shihong's army rose greatly in power, reaching more than a hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Shihong's force swelled to more than a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬辰，士弘自稱皇帝，國號楚，建元太平；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on renchen, Shihong proclaimed himself Emperor, state title Chu, era name Taiping;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day renchen, Lin Shihong declared himself emperor of Chu and adopted the era name Great Peace;

sentences.zh: 遂取九江、臨川、南康、宜昌等郡，豪傑爭殺隋守令，以郡縣應之。

translations.literal: he then took Jiujiang, Linchuan, Nankang, Yichang, and other commanderies; champions vied to kill Sui prefects and magistrates and submit their commanderies and counties to him.
translations.idiomatic: then seized Jiujiang, Linchuan, Nankang, Yichang, and other commanderies, as local strongmen raced to slaughter Sui officials and surrender their districts to him.

sentences.zh: 其地北自九江，南及番禺，皆為所有。

translations.literal: His territory ran from Jiujiang in the north to Panyu in the south—all was his possession.
translations.idiomatic: His domain stretched from Jiujiang in the north to Panyu in the south.

sentences.zh: 詔以右驍衛將軍唐公李淵為太原留守，以虎賁郎將王威、虎牙郎將高君雅為之副，將兵討甄翟兒，與翟兒遇於雀鼠谷。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Right Xiaowei General Duke of Tang Li Yuan as Taiyuan garrison commander, with Huben Lang Generals Wang Wei and Huya Lang General Gao Junya as his deputies, to lead troops against Zhen Zhai'er; they encountered Zhai'er at Sparrow-and-Rat Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named Li Yuan, Duke of Tang and Right Xiaowei General, commander of Taiyuan, with Wang Wei and Gao Junya as his deputies, and sent them against the rebel Zhen Zhai'er. They met at Sparrow-and-Rat Gorge.

sentences.zh: 淵眾才數千，賊圍淵數匝；

translations.literal: Yuan's force numbered only a few thousand; the bandits surrounded Yuan several times over;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan had only a few thousand men. The rebels ringed him round and round;

sentences.zh: 李世民將精兵救之，拔淵於萬眾之中，會步兵至，合擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Li Shimin led elite troops to rescue him, snatched Yuan out from amid ten thousand enemies; when the foot soldiers arrived, they joined attack and routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin led a picked force to the rescue, pulled his father free from the press of enemies, and when the infantry arrived they struck together and broke the rebels utterly.

sentences.zh: 帝疏薄骨肉，蔡王智積每不自安，及病，不呼醫，臨終，謂所親曰：「吾今日始知得保首領沒於地矣！」

translations.literal: The Emperor was cold and distant toward his kin; Prince of Cai Zhiji was always ill at ease. When he fell ill, he did not call for physicians; at the end, he said to those close to him: "Today I finally know I can keep my head and be buried in the earth!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept his own flesh and blood at arm's length. Prince of Cai Zhiji lived in constant dread. When illness took him, he refused physicians. On his deathbed he told those near him, "At last I know I shall keep my head and die in my own bed!"

sentences.zh: 張金稱、郝孝德、孫宣雅、高士達、楊公卿等寇掠河北，屠陷郡縣；

translations.literal: Zhang Jincheng, Hao Xiaode, Sun Xuanya, Gao Shida, Yang Gongqing, and others raided Hebei, slaughtering and capturing commanderies and counties;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jincheng, Hao Xiaode, Sun Xuanya, Gao Shida, Yang Gongqing, and others ravaged Hebei, sacking and slaughtering their way through town after town;

sentences.zh: 隋將帥敗亡者相繼，唯虎賁中郎將蒲城王辯、清河郡丞華陰楊善會數有功，善會前後與賊七百餘戰，未嘗負敗。

translations.literal: Sui generals fell in defeat one after another; only Huben Zhonglang General Wang Bian of Pucheng and Yang Shanhu of Huayin, magistrate of Qinghe Commandery, repeatedly achieved merit—Shanhui fought the bandits more than seven hundred times before and after, never once suffering defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Sui commanders fell in defeat one after another. Only Wang Bian of Pucheng, Huben Zhonglang General, and Yang Shanhu of Huayin, magistrate of Qinghe, won repeated victories—Shanhui fought the rebels more than seven hundred engagements and never lost.

sentences.zh: 帝遣太僕卿楊義臣討張金稱。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched Minister of Imperial Stud Yang Yichen to suppress Zhang Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yang Yichen, Minister of the Imperial Stud, to destroy Zhang Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 金稱營於平恩東北，義臣引兵直進抵臨清之西，據永濟渠為營，去金稱營四十里，深溝高壘，不與戰。

translations.literal: Jincheng camped northeast of Ping'en; Yichen led his army straight forward to the west of Linqing, established camp at the Yongji Canal, forty li from Jincheng's camp, dug deep trenches and raised high ramparts, and would not give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jincheng encamped northeast of Ping'en. Yang Yichen pushed west to Linqing, pitched camp on the Yongji Canal forty li away, dug deep trenches, raised high walls, and refused to fight.

sentences.zh: 金稱日引兵至義臣營西，義臣勒兵擐甲，約與之戰，既而不出。

translations.literal: Daily Jincheng led troops to the west of Yichen's camp; Yichen marshaled his troops in armor, pledged to fight—and then did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Every day Zhang Jincheng marched to the west of Yichen's camp. Yichen would muster his men in armor as if ready to give battle—and then stay inside.

sentences.zh: 日暮，金稱還營，明旦，復來；

translations.literal: At dusk Jincheng returned to camp; at dawn the next day, he came again;
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Jincheng withdrew; at dawn he returned;

sentences.zh: 如是月餘，義臣竟不出。

translations.literal: thus for more than a month, Yichen never came out.
translations.idiomatic: and so for more than a month Yang Yichen never emerged.

sentences.zh: 金稱以為怯，屢逼其營詈辱之。

translations.literal: Jincheng thought him cowardly and repeatedly pressed upon his camp with curses and insults.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jincheng decided he was a coward and repeatedly rode up to curse and taunt his camp.

sentences.zh: 義臣乃謂金稱曰：「汝明旦來，我當必戰。」

translations.literal: Yichen then said to Jincheng: "Tomorrow when you come, I shall certainly fight."
translations.idiomatic: At last Yichen sent word: "Come tomorrow, and I will fight you."

sentences.zh: 金稱易之，不復設備。

translations.literal: Jincheng took it lightly and no longer made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Jincheng took him at his word and relaxed his guard.

sentences.zh: 義臣簡精騎二千，夜自館陶濟河，伺金稱離營，即入擊其累重。

translations.literal: Yichen selected two thousand elite horsemen, crossed the river by night from Guantao, watched for Jincheng to leave camp, and immediately entered to strike his baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: Yichen chose two thousand crack horsemen, crossed the river by night from Guantao, waited until Jincheng marched out, then fell upon his baggage train.

sentences.zh: 金稱聞之，引兵還，義臣從後擊之，金稱大敗，與左右逃於清河之東。

translations.literal: Jincheng heard of it and led troops back; Yichen struck from behind; Jincheng was utterly defeated and fled east of the Qing River with a few companions.
translations.idiomatic: Jincheng turned back at the news. Yichen hit him from the rear. Jincheng was routed and fled east of the Qing River with a handful of followers.

sentences.zh: 月餘，楊善會討擒之。

translations.literal: More than a month later, Yang Shanhu captured him in a punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Yang Shanhu ran him down and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 吏立木於市，懸其頭，張其手足，令仇家割食之；

translations.literal: Officials erected a wooden stake in the market, hung his head, spread his limbs, and had the families of his victims carve and eat him;
translations.idiomatic: The authorities set up a post in the marketplace, hung his head, spread his limbs, and let the families of his victims cut flesh from his body and eat it;

sentences.zh: 未死間，歌謳不輟。

translations.literal: before he was dead, he kept singing without cease.
translations.idiomatic: and even as he died he would not stop singing.

sentences.zh: 詔以善會為清河通守。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Shanhui as general defender of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Shanhui general defender of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 涿郡通守郭絢將兵萬餘人討高士達。

translations.literal: Zhuo Commandery general defender Guo Xuan led more than ten thousand troops to suppress Gao Shida.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xuan, general defender of Zhuo Commandery, marched against Gao Shida with more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 士達自以才略不及竇建德，乃進建德為軍司馬，悉以兵授之。

translations.literal: Shida considered his own talent and stratagem inferior to Dou Jiande's; he therefore promoted Jiande to army marshal and entrusted all troops to him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shida knew himself no match in talent or strategy for Dou Jiande. He made Jiande army marshal and handed over command of all his forces.

sentences.zh: 建德請士達守輜重，自簡精兵七千人拒絢，詐為與士達有隙而叛，遣人請降於絢，願為前驅，擊士達以自效。

translations.literal: Jiande asked Shida to guard the baggage train, selected seven thousand elite troops himself to resist Xuan, feigned a rift with Shida and defected, sent men to offer surrender to Xuan, and volunteered to serve as vanguard and attack Shida to prove his worth.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande left Shida to guard the baggage, took seven thousand picked troops to face Guo Xuan, pretended to break with Shida and defect, sent envoys offering surrender, and promised to lead the van against Shida to prove his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 絢信之，引兵隨建德至長河，不復設備。

translations.literal: Xuan believed him, led troops following Jiande to Changhe, and no longer made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xuan believed him, followed Jiande to Changhe, and lowered his guard.

sentences.zh: 建德襲之，殺虜數千人，斬絢首，獻士達，張金稱餘眾皆歸建德。

translations.literal: Jiande struck him, killed and captured several thousand, cut off Xuan's head and presented it to Shida; the remnant forces of Zhang Jincheng all submitted to Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande turned on him, killed and captured several thousand, severed Xuan's head and sent it to Shida, and the remnants of Zhang Jincheng's band all rallied to Jiande.

sentences.zh: 楊義臣乘勝至平原，欲入高雞泊討之。

translations.literal: Yang Yichen pressed his victory to Pingyuan, intending to enter Gaojibo to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yichen pressed his advantage into Pingyuan, intending to drive into Gaojibo and finish them off.

sentences.zh: 建德謂士達曰：「歷觀隋將，善用兵者無如義臣。

translations.literal: Jiande said to Shida: "Surveying all Sui generals, none uses troops so well as Yichen.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande told Shida, "Of all Sui commanders, none handles an army like Yang Yichen.

sentences.zh: 今滅張金稱而來，其鋒不可當。

translations.literal: Now that he has destroyed Zhang Jincheng and is coming, his edge cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: He has just crushed Zhang Jincheng and is coming at us with momentum no one can meet head-on.

sentences.zh: 請引兵避之，使其欲戰不得，坐費歲月，將士疲倦。

translations.literal: I ask that we withdraw and avoid him, let him desire battle but gain none, passively consuming months until officers and soldiers grow weary.
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw and refuse battle. Let him burn to fight and find no foe. Wear away the months until his men are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 然後乘間擊之，乃可破也。

translations.literal: Then, seizing an opening, we strike him—and only then can he be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Then strike when the moment opens—and only then can we break him.

sentences.zh: 不然，恐非公之敵。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, I fear he is not an opponent your lordship can match."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I fear he is more than you can handle."

sentences.zh: 士達不從，留建德守營，自帥精兵逆擊義臣，戰小勝，因縱酒高宴。

translations.literal: Shida would not follow this; he left Jiande to guard camp, personally led elite troops to meet Yichen head-on, won a small victory, and thereupon gave himself to wine and a grand feast.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shida would not listen. He left Jiande to hold the camp, led his best troops out to meet Yichen, won a minor skirmish, and then gave himself over to wine and celebration.

sentences.zh: 建德聞之曰：「東海公未有破敵，遽自矜大，禍至不久矣！」

translations.literal: Jiande heard of it and said: "Lord Donghai has not yet broken the enemy yet already boasts grandly—disaster will arrive before long!"
translations.idiomatic: When Jiande heard, he said, "Lord Donghai has not broken the enemy and already struts like a conqueror. Ruin is close at hand."

sentences.zh: 後五日，義臣大破士達，於陳斬之，乘勝逐北，趣其營，營中守兵皆潰。

translations.literal: Five days later, Yichen utterly defeated Shida, beheaded him in formation, pressed the victory in pursuit north, hastened to his camp—the garrison defenders all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later Yang Yichen shattered Shida's army, cut off his head on the field, chased the rout to the camp, and the garrison fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 建德與百餘騎亡去，至饒陽，乘其無備，攻陷之，收兵，得三千餘人。

translations.literal: Jiande fled with a little over a hundred horsemen; reaching Raoyang, he took advantage of their unpreparedness, captured it, gathered troops, and obtained more than three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande escaped with a little over a hundred horsemen, seized Raoyang while it was undefended, and gathered more than three thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 義臣既殺士達，以為建德不足憂，引去。

translations.literal: Yichen, having killed Shida, considered Jiande not worth worrying about and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yichen, having killed Shida, dismissed Jiande as no further threat and marched away.

sentences.zh: 建德還平原，收士達散兵，收葬死者，為士達發喪，軍復大振，自稱將軍。

translations.literal: Jiande returned to Pingyuan, gathered Shida's scattered soldiers, collected and buried the dead, held funeral rites for Shida—the army again rose greatly, and he proclaimed himself General.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande returned to Pingyuan, rallied Shida's scattered men, buried the dead, and held funeral rites for Shida. His army swelled again, and he took the title of general.

sentences.zh: 先是，群盜得隋官及士族子弟，皆殺之，獨建德善遇之。

translations.literal: Previously, when bandit groups captured Sui officials and offspring of gentry families, they all killed them; only Jiande treated them well.
translations.idiomatic: Until then rebel bands had killed every Sui official and gentry hostage they took. Jiande alone treated such captives with kindness.

sentences.zh: 由是隋官稍以城降之，聲勢日盛，勝兵至十餘萬人。

translations.literal: Hence Sui officials gradually submitted cities to him; his fame and force daily swelled—battle-ready troops reached more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Sui officials therefore began surrendering their towns to him. His reputation and power grew day by day until his fighting force exceeded a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 內史侍郎虞世基以帝惡聞賊盜，諸將及郡縣有告敗求救者，世基皆抑損表狀，不以實聞，但云：「鼠竊狗盜，郡縣捕逐，行當殄盡，願陛下勿以介懷。」

translations.literal: Interior Secretary Vice-Minister Yu Shiji, knowing the Emperor hated to hear of bandits and robbers—for every general and commandery or county that reported defeat and begged aid—Shiji always diminished and curtailed the memorials, not reporting truthfully, but only saying: "Rat-thieves and dog-robbers—the commanderies and counties pursue and capture them; they will soon be exterminated—Your Majesty, pray do not take it to heart."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shiji, vice minister of the Secretariat, knew the emperor loathed reports of rebellion. Whenever generals or local officials sent word of defeat and begged for help, Shiji toned down their memorials and told the throne only this: "Petty thieves and scavengers—the districts are hunting them down and will soon wipe them out. Your Majesty need not trouble yourself."

sentences.zh: 帝良以為然，或杖其使者，以為妄言，由是盜賊遍海內，陷沒郡縣，帝皆弗之知也。

translations.literal: The Emperor fully assented; sometimes he even caned the messengers, deeming them wild talk—wherefore bandits and robbers spread throughout the land and commanderies and counties fell, yet the Emperor knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this gladly, and sometimes had the bearers of bad news beaten for spreading alarm. Rebels overran the empire and cities fell, while the emperor remained ignorant.

sentences.zh: 楊義臣破降河北賊數十萬，列狀上聞，帝歎曰：「我初不聞，賊頓如此，義臣降賊何多也！」

translations.literal: Yang Yichen broke and received the surrender of several hundred thousand Hebei bandits, submitting a detailed memorial to report this; the Emperor sighed and said: "At first I never heard of it—the bandits suddenly are like this! How many bandits has Yichen surrendered!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yichen crushed and accepted the surrender of several hundred thousand Hebei rebels and reported the fact in full, the emperor sighed and said, "I had no idea the rebels had grown so vast. Why has Yichen taken so many surrenders?"

sentences.zh: 世基對曰：「小竊雖多，未足為慮。

translations.literal: Shiji replied: "Though petty thieves are many, they are not worth concern.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji answered, "They are only small bands—nothing to worry over.

sentences.zh: 義臣克之，擁兵不少，久在閫外，此最非宜。」

translations.literal: Yichen has conquered them yet holds no small army, and long remains outside the gates—this is most improper."
translations.idiomatic: But Yichen now commands a large force and has long been away from court. That is what should trouble us."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿言是也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Your words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 遽追義臣，放散其兵，賊由是復盛。

translations.literal: At once he recalled Yang Yichen, discharged and dispersed his troops, and the bandits thereby flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately recalled Yang Yichen, disbanded his army, and the rebels surged back to strength.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史韋雲起劾奏：「世基及御史大夫裴蘊職典樞要，維持內外，四方告變，不為奏聞。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Attendant Censor Wei Yunqi impeached and memorialized: "Yu Shiji and Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun hold offices governing the pivot and key affairs, maintaining inner and outer affairs; when the four quarters report calamities and changes, they do not memorialize and report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Attendant Censor Wei Yunqi submitted an impeachment: "Yu Shiji and Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun hold the empire's most critical posts, yet when the provinces report rebellion they fail to inform Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 賊數實多，裁減言少，陛下既聞賊少，發兵不多，眾寡懸殊，往皆不克，故使官軍失利，賊黨日滋。

translations.literal: The bandits' numbers are in truth many, yet they trim and reduce the reports to say few; since Your Majesty has heard the bandits are few, the troops sent are not many; the masses are vastly unequal, and in the past all failed to conquer—therefore causing the official army to lose advantage, and the bandit factions daily to increase.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels are far more numerous than they admit, yet the memorials are cut down to make them seem small. Believing this, Your Majesty sends too few troops against overwhelming odds; the government forces lose battle after battle, and rebel ranks swell daily.

sentences.zh: 請付有司結正其罪。」

translations.literal: I request that they be handed over to the responsible offices to settle and determine their crimes."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that they be turned over to the proper authorities for judgment."

sentences.zh: 大理卿鄭善果奏：「雲起詆訾名臣，所言不實，非毀朝政，妄作威權。」

translations.literal: Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Zheng Shanguo memorialized: "Yunqi slanders and reviles famous ministers; what he says is not true—it is not to destroy court governance, but to presumptuously wield authority and power."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Judge Zheng Shanguo replied: "Wei Yunqi has slandered eminent ministers with false charges. This is not honest criticism of the court but an abuse of power."

sentences.zh: 由是左遷雲起為大理司直。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yunqi was demoted and transferred to be Directing Secretary of the Court of Judicial Review."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yunqi was demoted to Directing Secretary in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 帝至江都，江、淮郡官謁見者，專問禮餉豐薄，豐則超遷丞、守，薄則率從停解。

translations.literal: When the Emperor arrived at Jiangdu, among the Jiang and Huai commandery officials who came to pay respects, he asked only whether their tribute gifts were rich or poor; if rich, they were promoted beyond rank to assistant or prefect; if poor, they were demoted or dismissed along with their followers.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang reached Jiangdu, the local officials who came to pay their respects were judged solely on the lavishness of their gifts. Generous tribute won swift promotion to assistant prefect or prefect; meager gifts brought demotion or dismissal.

sentences.zh: 江都郡丞王世充獻銅鏡屏風，遷通守；

translations.literal: Jiangdu Commandery Assistant Wang Shichong presented a copper-mirror screen; he was promoted to Vice Prefect;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong, assistant prefect of Jiangdu, offered a folding screen set with bronze mirrors and was made vice prefect;

sentences.zh: 歷陽郡丞趙元楷獻異味，遷江都郡丞。

translations.literal: Liyang Commandery Assistant Zhao Yuankai presented exotic delicacies and was promoted to Jiangdu Commandery Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yuankai, assistant prefect of Liyang, sent rare delicacies and was appointed assistant prefect of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 由是郡縣競務刻剝，以充貢獻。

translations.literal: Thereupon commanderies and counties competed in striving to exploit and strip, to fill their tribute offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies and counties raced to squeeze the people dry in order to meet the tribute demands.

sentences.zh: 民外為盜賊所掠，內為郡縣所賦，生計無遺；

translations.literal: The people, outwardly plundered by bandits and robbers, inwardly taxed by commanderies and counties, had nothing left for livelihood;
translations.idiomatic: The people were robbed by bandits without and taxed by officials within, until nothing remained of their livelihood;

sentences.zh: 加之饑饉無食，民始采樹皮葉，或搗稿為末，或煮土而食之，諸物皆盡，乃自相食；

translations.literal: Added to this was famine with no food; the people first gathered tree bark and leaves, or pounded straw into powder, or boiled earth and ate it; when all things were exhausted, they then ate one another;
translations.idiomatic: Famine followed. People stripped bark and leaves from trees, ground straw into meal, or boiled clay to eat. When every substitute was gone, they turned to cannibalism;

sentences.zh: 而官食猶充牣，吏皆畏法，莫敢振救。

translations.literal: Yet official stores of grain still overflowed and filled the bins; the clerks all feared the law, and none dared to relieve and save.
translations.idiomatic: Yet government granaries remained full, and the officials, fearing the law, dared not open them to save the starving.

sentences.zh: 王世充密為帝簡閱江淮民間美女獻之，由是益有寵。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong secretly selected and reviewed beautiful women among the Jiang and Huai populace and presented them to the Emperor; thereby he gained even greater favor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong secretly searched out beautiful women across the Jiang-Huai region and sent them to the emperor, winning still greater favor at court.

sentences.zh: 河間賊帥格謙擁眾十餘萬，據豆子，自稱燕王，帝命王世充將兵討斬之。

translations.literal: Hejian bandit chief Ge Qian gathered a host of more than one hundred thousand, occupied Douzi, styled himself King of Yan; the Emperor ordered Wang Shichong to lead troops to suppress and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Qian, a rebel leader from Hejian, mustered more than a hundred thousand men, seized Douzi, and proclaimed himself King of Yan. Emperor Yang ordered Wang Shichong to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 謙將勃海高開道收其餘眾，寇掠燕地，軍勢復振。

translations.literal: Qian's general Gao Kaidao of Bohai gathered his remaining host, raided and plundered the Yan region, and the army's momentum revived.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Qian's lieutenant Gao Kaidao of Bohai rallied the survivors, raided across Yan, and restored the rebels' strength.

sentences.zh: 初，帝謀伐高麗，器械資儲，皆積於涿郡；

translations.literal: Initially, when the Emperor planned to attack Goguryeo, weapons, equipment, and supplies were all stored at Zhuo Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Yang prepared his campaign against Goguryeo, arms and supplies had been stockpiled at Zhuo Commandery;

sentences.zh: 涿郡人物殷阜，屯兵數萬。

translations.literal: Zhuo Commandery was rich in men and goods, with tens of thousands of troops encamped.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery was populous and prosperous, garrisoned by tens of thousands of soldiers.

sentences.zh: 又，臨朔宮多珍寶，諸賊競來侵掠；

translations.literal: Moreover, Linshuo Palace held many precious treasures, and the various bandits competed to come and raid and plunder;
translations.idiomatic: Linshuo Palace held great stores of treasure, and rebels flocked to plunder it;

sentences.zh: 留守官虎賁郎將趙什住等不能拒，唯虎賁郎將雲陽羅藝獨出戰，前後破賊甚眾，威名日重，什住等陰忌之。

translations.literal: The garrison officials, Tiger Guard Commandants Zhao Shizhu and others, could not repel them; only Tiger Guard Commandant Luo Yi of Yunyang alone went out to fight, and before and after broke many bandits; his renown daily grew heavy, and Shizhu and the others secretly envied him.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commanders Zhao Shizhu and his colleagues could not hold them off. Only Luo Yi, a Tiger Guard commandant from Yunyang, took the field alone, crushing rebel bands again and again until his fame grew daily—and Shizhu and the others secretly resented him.

sentences.zh: 藝將作亂，先宣言以激其眾曰：「吾輩討賊數有功，城中倉庫山積，制在留守之官，而莫肯散施以濟貧乏，將何以勸將士！」

translations.literal: Yi was about to raise rebellion; he first proclaimed to stir his host, saying: "We have repeatedly had merit in suppressing bandits; the city stores and granaries are piled like mountains, controlled by the garrison officials, yet they will not open and distribute to relieve the poor and needy—how are we to encourage officers and soldiers!"
translations.idiomatic: Planning a revolt, Luo Yi first roused his men with a proclamation: "We have fought bandits with repeated success, yet the city granaries overflow while the garrison officers refuse to share with the starving. How can such men inspire loyalty?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆憤怨。

translations.literal: The host all grew angry and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers burned with anger.

sentences.zh: 軍還，郡丞出城候藝，藝因執之，陳兵而入。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the commandery assistant went out of the city to await Yi; Yi thereupon seized him, arrayed troops, and entered.
translations.idiomatic: When the troops returned, the assistant prefect came out to greet Luo Yi. Yi seized him, marched his soldiers into the city, and took control.

sentences.zh: 什住等懼，皆來聽命，乃發庫物以賜戰士，開倉廩以賑貧乏，境內鹹悅；

translations.literal: Shizhu and the others were afraid and all came to obey; then he opened the storehouses and distributed goods to reward the warriors, opened the granaries to relieve the poor and needy, and throughout the territory all were pleased;
translations.idiomatic: Shizhu and the rest submitted in fear. Luo Yi opened the treasuries to reward his soldiers and the granaries to feed the poor, winning the people's approval throughout the region;

sentences.zh: 殺不同己者勃海太守唐禕等數人，威振燕地，柳城、懷遠並歸之。

translations.literal: He killed several who did not agree with him, including Bohai Prefect Tang Yi; his authority shook the Yan region, and Liucheng and Huaiyuan both submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He executed several dissenters, including Bohai Prefect Tang Yi, and his power spread across Yan. Liucheng and Huaiyuan both joined him.

sentences.zh: 藝黜柳城太守楊林甫，改郡為營州，以襄平太守鄧暠為總管，藝自稱幽州總管。

translations.literal: Yi removed Liucheng Prefect Yang Linfu, changed the commandery to Ying Prefecture, appointed Xiangping Prefect Deng Gao as overall commander, and Yi styled himself Overall Commander of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yi deposed Yang Linfu as prefect of Liucheng, reorganized the district as Ying Prefecture, named Deng Gao of Xiangping as its commander, and took for himself the title Overall Commander of You Province.

sentences.zh: 突厥數寇北連。

translations.literal: The Turks repeatedly raided the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks raided the northern frontier again and again.

sentences.zh: 詔晉陽留守李淵帥太原道兵與馬邑太守王仁恭擊之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jinyang Garrison Commander Li Yuan to lead the Taiyuan Circuit troops together with Mayi Prefect Wang Rengong to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Li Yuan, garrison commander at Jinyang, to lead the Taiyuan circuit army with Mayi Prefect Wang Rengong against them.

sentences.zh: 時突厥方強，兩軍眾不滿五千，仁恭患之。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks were just then strong; the two armies together numbered fewer than five thousand, and Rengong was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks were at the height of their power, and the combined force numbered fewer than five thousand men. Wang Rengong was deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 淵選善騎射者二千人，使之飲食捨止一如突厥，或與突厥遇，則伺便擊之，前後屢捷，突厥頗憚之。

translations.literal: Yuan selected two thousand skilled horsemen and archers, had them eat, drink, lodge, and halt just like the Turks; when they occasionally met Turks, they watched for an opportunity and struck; before and after they repeatedly won victories, and the Turks came greatly to fear them.
