translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan picked two thousand expert mounted archers and trained them to live and march like Turks. Whenever they encountered Turk raiders they seized the moment to attack, winning victory after victory until the Turks learned to fear them.

sentences.zh: 恭皇帝上

translations.literal: Emperor Gong, Part One.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gong, Part One

sentences.zh: 春，正月，右御衛將軍陳稜討杜伏威，伏威帥眾拒之。

translations.literal: Spring, first month: Right Imperial Guard General Chen Leng suppressed Du Fuwei; Fuwei led his host to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Right Imperial Guard General Chen Leng marched against Du Fuwei, who met him at the head of his army.

sentences.zh: 稜閉壁不戰，伏威遺以婦人之服，謂之「陳姥」。

translations.literal: Leng closed his walls and would not fight; Fuwei sent him women's garments, calling him "Old Mother Chen."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Leng shut himself in his camp and refused battle. Du Fuwei sent him women's clothing and mocked him as "Old Mother Chen."

sentences.zh: 稜怒，出戰，伏威奮出，大破之，稜僅以身免。

translations.literal: Leng grew angry, came out to fight; Fuwei charged forth with vigor and greatly broke him; Leng barely escaped with his person alone.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Chen Leng sallied out to fight. Du Fuwei charged hard and routed him completely. Chen Leng escaped with nothing but his life.

sentences.zh: 伏威乘勝破高郵，引兵據歷陽，自稱總管，以輔公祏為長史，分遣諸將徇屬縣，所至輒下，江淮間小盜爭附之。

translations.literal: Fuwei rode the victory to break Gaoyou, led troops to occupy Liyang, styled himself Overall Commander, appointed Fu Gongshi as Chief Clerk, and separately dispatched generals to subdue subordinate counties; wherever they arrived they were taken, and the small bandits between the Jiang and Huai competed to attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fuwei pressed his advantage, seized Gaoyou, and established himself at Liyang as self-declared overall commander, with Fu Gongshi as chief clerk. He sent his generals to subdue neighboring counties, which fell one after another, and petty bandits across the Jiang-Huai region flocked to his banner.

sentences.zh: 伏威常選取死之士五千人，謂之「上募」，寵遇甚厚，有攻戰，輒令上募先擊之，戰罷閱視，有傷在背者即殺之，以其退而被擊故也。

translations.literal: Fuwei regularly selected five thousand death-dedicated warriors, calling them the "Elite Levy"; he favored and treated them very generously. When there was an attack or battle, he always had the Elite Levy strike first; when the battle ended he inspected them, and any with wounds on the back he immediately killed, because they had retreated and been struck from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fuwei maintained five thousand picked warriors called the "Elite Levy," whom he favored lavishly. In every battle they led the assault. Afterward he inspected the survivors and executed any man wounded in the back, treating retreat as cowardice punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 所獲資財，皆以賞軍。

translations.literal: All goods and wealth captured were used to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: All captured wealth went to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 士有戰死者，以妻、妾徇葬。

translations.literal: When a soldier died in battle, his wife or concubine was sacrificed for burial.
translations.idiomatic: When a soldier fell in battle, his wife or concubine was buried with him.

sentences.zh: 故人自為戰，所向無敵。

translations.literal: "Therefore men fought of their own accord, and wherever they went none could match them."
translations.idiomatic: "His men fought as if for their own lives, and his army seemed invincible."

sentences.zh: 丙辰，竇建德為壇於樂壽，自稱長樂王，置百官，改元丁丑。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Dou Jiande erected an altar at Leshou, styled himself King of Changle, established the hundred officials, and changed the era name to Dingchou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Dou Jiande raised an altar at Leshou, proclaimed himself King of Changle, appointed a full court, and declared a new reign era, Dingchou.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，魯郡賊帥徐圓朗攻陷東平，分兵略地，自琅邪以西，北至東平，盡有之，勝兵二萬餘人。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Lu Commandery bandit chief Xu Yuanlang attacked and captured Dongping, divided troops to seize territory; from Langye westward, north to Dongping, he possessed it all, with more than twenty thousand battle-ready soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Xu Yuanlang, a rebel leader from Lu Commandery, took Dongping and sent columns to seize the land from Langye in the west to Dongping in the north. He commanded more than twenty thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 盧明月轉掠河南，至於淮北，眾號四十萬，自稱無上王；

translations.literal: Lu Mingyue turned to raid Henan, reaching north of the Huai; his host was proclaimed at four hundred thousand, and he styled himself the Unsurpassed King;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Mingyue swept through Henan as far as the Huai River's north bank, claiming four hundred thousand followers and proclaiming himself the Unsurpassed King;

sentences.zh: 帝命江都通守王世充討之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Jiangdu Vice Prefect Wang Shichong to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang ordered Wang Shichong, vice prefect of Jiangdu, to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 世充與戰於南陽，大破之，斬明月，餘眾皆散。

translations.literal: Shichong fought him at Nanyang, greatly broke him, beheaded Mingyue, and the remaining host all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong met him at Nanyang, crushed his army, killed Lu Mingyue, and the survivors scattered.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬午，朔方鷹揚郎將梁師都殺郡丞唐世宗，據郡，自稱大丞相，北連突厥。

translations.literal: Second month, on renwu, Shuofang Eagle-Flight Commandant Liang Shidu killed Commandery Assistant Tang Shizong, seized the commandery, styled himself Grand Chancellor, and allied with the Turks to the north.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renwu, Liang Shidu, an Eagle-Flight commandant at Shuofang, killed Assistant Prefect Tang Shizong, seized the commandery, declared himself Grand Chancellor, and allied with the Turks in the north.

sentences.zh: 馬邑太守王仁恭，多受貨賂，不能振施。

translations.literal: Mayi Prefect Wang Rengong accepted many bribes and goods, and could not relieve and distribute aid.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rengong, prefect of Mayi, took bribes freely and never opened his stores to help the people.

sentences.zh: 郡人劉武周，驍勇喜任俠，為鷹揚府校尉。

translations.literal: A man of the commandery, Liu Wuzhou, was fierce and brave and delighted in chivalrous deeds; he served as Eagle-Flight Guard company commander.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou, a local man famed for courage and boldness, held the rank of company commander in the Eagle-Flight Guard.

sentences.zh: 仁恭以其土豪，甚親厚之，令帥親兵屯閣下。

translations.literal: Rengong, because he was a local strongman, treated him very closely and generously, and ordered him to lead personal troops encamped below the pavilion gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rengong, recognizing him as a local power, treated him with great favor and stationed him below the gate with a personal guard.

sentences.zh: 武周與仁恭侍兒私通，恐事洩，謀作亂，先宣言曰：「今百姓饑饉，殭屍滿道，王府君閉倉不賑恤，豈為民父母之意乎！」

translations.literal: Wuzhou had a secret affair with Rengong's serving maid; fearing the matter would leak, he plotted rebellion and first proclaimed, saying: "Now the people suffer famine; corpses fill the roads. Prefect Wang closes the granaries and will not relieve and succor—can this be the intent of parents to the people!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou was sleeping with Wang Rengong's maid. Fearing exposure, he plotted rebellion and first spread word among the people: "Famine stalks the land and corpses choke the roads, yet Prefect Wang keeps the granaries shut. Is this how a ruler should treat his people?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆憤怒。

translations.literal: The host all grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd erupted in fury.

sentences.zh: 武周稱疾臥家，豪傑來候問，武周椎牛縱酒，因大言曰：「壯士豈能坐待溝壑！

translations.literal: Wuzhou claimed illness and lay at home; bold heroes came to inquire after him; Wuzhou slaughtered an ox and poured wine freely, and thereupon spoke boldly, saying: "Can bold warriors sit and wait for the ditches and gullies!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou feigned illness at home. When local leaders came to visit, he slaughtered an ox, opened the wine, and declared: "Are brave men to sit idle while starvation kills us?

sentences.zh: 今倉粟爛積，誰能與我共取之？」

translations.literal: Now the granary grain rots in piled heaps—who will join me in taking it together?"
translations.idiomatic: The granaries overflow with grain going to waste. Who will join me in seizing it?"

sentences.zh: 豪傑皆許諾。

translations.literal: The bold heroes all promised assent.
translations.idiomatic: They all pledged themselves.

sentences.zh: 己丑，仁恭坐聽事，武周上謁，其黨張萬歲等隨入，升階，斬仁恭，持其首出徇，郡中無敢動者。

translations.literal: On jichou, Rengong sat in the audience hall; Wuzhou went up to pay respects; his partisans Zhang Wansui and others followed in, ascended the steps, beheaded Rengong, carried his head out to display in procession, and in the commandery none dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Wang Rengong was holding court when Liu Wuzhou came to pay his respects. Zhang Wansui and the other conspirators followed him inside, mounted the steps, and cut Wang Rengong down. They paraded his head through the city, and no one dared move against them.

sentences.zh: 於是開倉以賑饑民，馳檄境內屬城，皆下之，收兵得萬餘人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he opened the granaries to relieve the starving people, sent urgent proclamations to subordinate cities within the territory, and all submitted; gathering troops he obtained more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the granaries to feed the hungry, sent summons throughout the district, and one city after another submitted. Within days he had more than ten thousand men under arms.

sentences.zh: 武周自稱太守，遣使附於突厥。

translations.literal: Wuzhou styled himself Prefect and sent envoys to attach himself to the Turks."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou declared himself prefect and sent envoys to submit to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 李密說翟讓曰：「今東都空虛，兵不素練；

translations.literal: Li Mi persuaded Zhai Rang, saying: "Now the Eastern Capital is empty and hollow; the troops are not by nature trained;
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi said to Zhai Rang: "The Eastern Capital is weakly defended and its soldiers are poorly trained;

sentences.zh: 越王沖幼，留守諸官政令不壹，士民離心。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Chong is young; the various garrison officials' government orders are not unified, and officers and people are estranged in heart.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Yue is a child; the garrison officials cannot agree on policy; soldiers and civilians alike have lost heart.

sentences.zh: 段達、元文都，暗而無謀。

translations.literal: Duan Da and Yuan Wendu are dull and without strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da and Yuan Wendu are obtuse men without a plan among them.

sentences.zh: 以僕料之，彼非將軍之敵。

translations.literal: By my reckoning, they are not the General's match.
translations.idiomatic: In my judgment they are no match for you, General.

sentences.zh: 若將軍能用僕計，天下可指麾而定也。」

translations.literal: If the General can use my plan, the realm can be settled at a wave of the hand and a command."
translations.idiomatic: If you follow my plan, the empire can be won with a gesture."

sentences.zh: 乃遣其黨裴叔方覘東都虛實，留守官司覺之，始為守禦之備，且馳表告江都。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent his partisan Pei Shufang to reconnoiter the Eastern Capital's strength and weakness; the garrison officials detected it, and only then made defensive preparations, and also sent urgent memorials to report to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his follower Pei Shufang to spy out the capital's defenses. The garrison detected the plot, began preparing for siege, and dispatched urgent reports to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 密謂讓曰：「事勢如此，不可不發。

translations.literal: Mi said to Rang: "The situation is thus; we cannot fail to act.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi told Zhai Rang: "Matters have come to this—we must strike at once.

sentences.zh: 兵法曰：『先則制於己，後則制於人。』

translations.literal: The art of war says: 'He who acts first controls the initiative for himself; he who acts later is controlled by others.'
translations.idiomatic: The art of war says: 'He who moves first holds the advantage; he who moves second is at another's mercy.'

sentences.zh: 今百姓饑饉，洛口倉多積粟，去都百里有餘，將軍若親帥大眾，輕行掩襲，彼遠未能救，又先無豫備，取之如拾遺耳。

translations.literal: Now the people suffer famine; Luokou Granary stores much accumulated grain, more than a hundred li from the capital. If the General personally leads the great host in a light, swift surprise raid, they are far and cannot rescue in time, and beforehand have no prepared defenses—taking it would be like picking up what others have dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The people are starving, and Luokou Granary, a hundred li from the capital, holds vast stores of grain. If you lead the main force in a swift surprise attack, the capital cannot relieve it in time and will be caught unprepared. Seizing it would be as easy as picking up something dropped on the road.

sentences.zh: 比其聞知，吾已獲之，發粟以賑窮乏，遠近孰不歸附！

translations.literal: By the time they hear and know, we will already have taken it; opening grain to relieve the poor and destitute—near and far, who would not submit and attach!
translations.idiomatic: Before word even reaches the capital we will hold the granary, open the stores to feed the hungry, and who near or far would not flock to us!

sentences.zh: 百萬之眾，一朝可集，枕威養銳，以逸待勞。

translations.literal: A host of a million can in one morning be gathered; resting on authority and nurturing sharpness, awaiting the weary with ease.
translations.idiomatic: A million men can be gathered in a single day. We will hold our strength, rest our troops, and meet their exhausted armies fresh.

sentences.zh: 縱彼能來，吾有備矣。

translations.literal: Even if they can come, we will already have prepared defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they come against us, we will be ready.

sentences.zh: 然後檄召四方，引賢豪而資計策，選驍悍而授兵柄，除亡隋之社稷，布將軍之政令，豈不盛哉！」

translations.literal: Then issuing proclamations to summon the four quarters, drawing worthy heroes to supply plans and stratagems, selecting fierce and bold men and entrusting them with military authority, removing the fallen Sui dynasty's altars of soil and grain, and spreading the General's government orders—would this not be magnificent!"
translations.idiomatic: Then we can summon the realm by proclamation, gather wise and bold men for counsel, put fierce fighters in command, overthrow the dying Sui, and establish your rule throughout the land. What glory could surpass that!"

sentences.zh: 讓曰：「此英雄之略，非僕所堪；

translations.literal: Rang said: "This is a hero's grand strategy—not what I am fit for;
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang replied: "That is a hero's strategy, beyond my ability;

sentences.zh: 惟君之命，盡力從事，請君先發，僕為後殿。」

translations.literal: only obey your command; I will exert my strength and follow the undertaking. I ask you to advance first; I will serve as the rear guard."
translations.idiomatic: but I will obey your command with all my strength. You go first; I will cover the rear."

sentences.zh: 庚寅，密、讓將精兵七千人出陽城北，逾方山，自羅口襲興浴倉，破之；

translations.literal: On gengyin, Mi and Rang led seven thousand elite troops out north of Yangcheng, crossed Mount Fang, and from Luokou raided Xingluo Granary and broke it;
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Li Mi and Zhai Rang led seven thousand elite troops out north of Yangcheng, crossed Mount Fang, and stormed Xingluo Granary from Luokou, taking it by assault;

sentences.zh: 開倉恣民所取，老弱襁負，道路相屬。

translations.literal: They opened the granary and let the people take as they wished; old and weak, carrying infants on their backs, lined the roads one after another."
translations.idiomatic: They opened the granaries and let the people take what they needed. The old and weak, babies on their backs, filled the roads in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 朝散大夫時德睿以尉氏應密，前宿城令祖君彥自昌平往歸之。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Shide Rui of Weishi responded to Mi; former Su Prefect Zu Junyan came from Changping to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Shide Rui of Weishi rallied to Li Mi, and Zu Junyan, former magistrate of Su, came from Changping to join him as well.

sentences.zh: 君彥，珽之子也，博學強記，文辭贍敏，著名海內，吏部侍郎薛道衡嘗薦之於高祖，高祖曰：「是歌殺斛律明月人兒邪？

translations.literal: Junyan was the son of Ting; he was broadly learned with a strong memory, his literary phrasing rich and quick, famous throughout the realm. Ministry of Personnel Vice-Minister Xue Daoheng once recommended him to Emperor Gaozu; Gaozu said: "Is this not the son of the man who composed the song that killed Hulu Mingyue?
translations.idiomatic: Zu Junyan was the son of Zu Ting, a man of vast learning and retentive memory, whose eloquent writing had won fame across the empire. Vice Minister of Personnel Xue Daoheng once recommended him to Emperor Gaozu, who said, "Is this not the son of the man whose poem destroyed Hulu Mingyue?

sentences.zh: 朕不須此輩！」

translations.literal: We have no need of such men!"
translations.idiomatic: I want no part of such men!"

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，尤疾其名，依常調選東平書佐，檢校宿城令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he especially hated Junyan's name; by regular rotation he was selected as a clerical assistant at Dongping and acting magistrate of Su.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne he hated Zu Junyan's reputation above all. Through routine appointment he was posted as a clerical aide at Dongping and acting magistrate of Su.

sentences.zh: 君彥自負其才，常鬱鬱思亂。

translations.literal: Junyan, confident in his talent, was often depressed and brooded on rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Junyan, proud of his gifts, brooded in frustration and longed for turmoil.

sentences.zh: 密素聞其名，得之大喜，引為上客，軍中書檄，悉以委之。

translations.literal: Mi had long heard his name; upon obtaining him he was greatly pleased, received him as a honored guest, and entrusted him with all military proclamations and dispatches."
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi had long known his name and was overjoyed to have him. He treated Zu Junyan as an honored guest and entrusted him with all the army's proclamations and dispatches.

sentences.zh: 越王侗遣虎賁郎將劉長恭、光祿少卿房崱帥步騎二萬五千討密。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Tong dispatched Tiger Guard Commandant Liu Changgong and Palace Provisioner Vice-Minister Fang Ke to lead twenty-five thousand infantry and cavalry to suppress Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yue Tong sent Tiger Guard Commandant Liu Changgong and Vice Minister of the Palace Provision Fang Ke with twenty-five thousand foot and horse to destroy Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 時東都人皆以密為饑賊盜米，烏合易破，爭來應募，國子三館學士及貴勝親戚皆來從軍，器械修整，衣服鮮華，旌旗鉦鼓甚盛。

translations.literal: At that time the people of the Eastern Capital all regarded Mi as famine bandits stealing grain—a mob easily broken—and competed to come enlist; academicians of the three halls of the Imperial Academy and noble and eminent kin all came to join the army; weapons and equipment were polished, clothing bright and splendid, banners, bells, and drums very grand.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the Eastern Capital took Li Mi for a band of starving grain thieves—a rabble easily scattered—and volunteers flooded the recruiting offices. Scholars from the Imperial Academy and sons of great families enlisted in droves, turning out with polished arms, bright clothing, and banners and drums in splendid array.

sentences.zh: 長恭等當其前，使河南討捕使裴仁基等將所部兵自汜水西入以掩其後，約十一日會於倉城南，密、讓具知其計。

translations.literal: Changgong and the others would face them from the front; he ordered Henan Pursuit Commissioner Pei Renji and others to lead their respective troops to enter from west of Sishui and strike their rear; they agreed to meet on the eleventh day south of the granary city. Mi and Rang knew the plan in full.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changgong would advance from the front while Pursuit Commissioner Pei Renji of Henan led his troops in from west of Sishui to take Li Mi from the rear. They planned to rendezvous south of the granary city on the eleventh day. Li Mi and Zhai Rang learned the whole scheme.

sentences.zh: 東都兵先至，士卒未朝食，長恭等驅之渡洛水，陳於石子河西，南北十餘里。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital troops arrived first; the soldiers had not yet eaten the morning meal; Changgong and the others drove them across the Luo River and arrayed them west of the Shizi River, north to south for more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital army arrived first. The men had not yet eaten breakfast when Liu Changgong drove them across the Luo River and formed battle lines west of the Shizi River, stretching more than ten li north to south.

sentences.zh: 密、讓選驍雄，分為十隊，令四隊伏橫嶺下以待仁基，以六隊陳於石子河東。

translations.literal: Mi and Rang selected fierce champions and divided them into ten companies; they ordered four companies to lie in ambush below Hengling to await Renji, and six companies to array east of the Shizi River.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi and Zhai Rang picked their best fighters and divided them into ten companies. Four lay in ambush below Hengling Ridge to wait for Pei Renji; six formed up east of the Shizi River.

sentences.zh: 長恭等見密兵少，輕之。

translations.literal: Changgong and the others saw Mi's troops were few and treated them lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changgong saw how few men Li Mi had and despised him.

sentences.zh: 讓先接戰，不利，密帥麾下橫衝之。

translations.literal: Rang first joined battle; it went badly, and Mi led his personal followers in a lateral charge against them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang opened the fight and faltered. Li Mi then led his personal guard in a sweeping charge.

sentences.zh: 隋兵饑疲，遂大敗，長恭等解衣潛竄得免，奔還東都，士卒死者什五六。

translations.literal: The Sui troops, hungry and weary, were thereupon greatly broken; Changgong and the others stripped their garments and secretly fled to escape, running back to the Eastern Capital; of the soldiers, five or six in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui soldiers, hungry and exhausted, broke completely. Liu Changgong and his officers stripped off their armor and fled in secret back to the Eastern Capital. Five or six soldiers in ten were killed.

sentences.zh: 越王侗釋長恭等罪，慰撫之。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Tong released Changgong and the others from guilt and comforted and reassured them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yue Tong pardoned Liu Changgong and the other commanders and tried to restore their spirits.

sentences.zh: 密、讓盡收其輜重器甲，威聲大振。

translations.literal: Mi and Rang fully gathered their baggage trains, weapons, and armor; their authority and renown greatly shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi and Zhai Rang captured all their supplies, weapons, and armor, and their fame resounded across the land.

sentences.zh: 讓於是推密為王，上密號為魏公；

translations.literal: Rang thereupon pushed Mi to be king and elevated Mi with the title Duke of Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang thereupon urged Li Mi to take royal rank and proclaimed him Duke of Wei;

sentences.zh: 庚子，設壇場，即位，稱元年，大赦。

translations.literal: On gengzi, he set up an altar platform, ascended the throne, styled the first year, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi he raised an altar, took the throne, declared a new reign year, and granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 其文書行下，稱行軍元帥府；

translations.literal: His documents issued downward were styled the Campaign Marshal's Office;
translations.idiomatic: His orders went out in the name of the Campaign Marshal's Office;

sentences.zh: 其魏公府置三司、六衛，元帥府置長史以下官屬。

translations.literal: His Duke of Wei Office established the Three Departments and Six Guards; the Marshal's Office established Chief Clerk and subordinate officials below.
translations.idiomatic: the Duke of Wei's court was organized with the Three Departments and Six Guards, and the marshal's staff with a chief clerk and full bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 拜翟讓為上柱國、司徒、東郡公，亦置長史以下官，減元帥府之半；

translations.literal: He appointed Zhai Rang as Pillar of State, Minister of Education, and Duke of Dong Commandery, also establishing Chief Clerk and subordinate officials, half the scale of the Marshal's Office;
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang was made Pillar of State, Minister of Education, and Duke of Dong Commandery, with a staff half the size of the marshal's own;

sentences.zh: 以單雄信為左武候大將軍，徐世勣為右武候大將軍，各領所部；

translations.literal: He made Shan Xiongxin Left Martial Guard General and Xu Shiji Right Martial Guard General, each commanding his respective division;
translations.idiomatic: Shan Xiongxin was named Left Martial Guard General and Xu Shiji Right Martial Guard General, each commanding his own forces;

sentences.zh: 房彥藻為元帥左長史，東郡邴元真為右長史，楊德方為左司馬，鄭德韜為右司馬，祖君彥為記室，其餘封拜各有差。

translations.literal: Fang Yanzao as Marshal's Left Chief Clerk, Bing Yuanzhen of Dong Commandery as Right Chief Clerk, Yang Defang as Left Major, Zheng Detao as Right Major, Zu Junyan as Recorder—the rest received enfeoffments and appointments each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yanzao became left chief clerk of the marshal's staff, Bing Yuanzhen of Dong Commandery right chief clerk, Yang Defang left major, Zheng Detao right major, and Zu Junyan recorder; the rest received titles and posts according to merit.

sentences.zh: 於是趙、魏以南，江、淮以北，群盜莫不響應，孟讓、郝孝德、王德仁及濟陰房獻伯、上谷王君廓、長平李士才、淮陽魏六兒、李德謙、譙郡張遷、魏郡李文相、譙郡黑社、白社、濟北張青特、上洛周北洮、胡驢賊等皆歸密。

translations.literal: Thereupon south of Zhao and Wei, north of the Jiang and Huai, none among the bandit hosts failed to respond; Meng Rang, Hao Xiaode, Wang Deren, and Fang Xianbo of Jiyin, Wang Junkuo of Shanggu, Li Shicai of Changping, Wei Liu'er of Huaiyang, Li Deqian, Zhang Qian of Qiao Commandery, Li Wenxiang of Wei Commandery, the Black Society and White Society of Qiao Commandery, Zhang Qingte of Jibei, Zhou Beitao of Shangluo, the Hu Donkey Bandits, and others all submitted to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhao and Wei south to the Jiang and Huai north, rebel bands answered his call one after another. Meng Rang, Hao Xiaode, Wang Deren, Fang Xianbo of Jiyin, Wang Junkuo of Shanggu, Li Shicai of Changping, Wei Liu'er of Huaiyang, Li Deqian, Zhang Qian of Qiao, Li Wenxiang of Wei, the Black Society and White Society of Qiao, Zhang Qingte of Jibei, Zhou Beitao of Shangluo, the Hu Donkey Bandits, and many others all joined Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 密悉拜官爵，使各鄰其眾，置百營簿以領之。

translations.literal: Mi fully bestowed offices and ranks, had each neighbor his own host, and established a register of the hundred camps to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi enfeoffed them all with titles and posts, set each to command his own followers, and kept a register of the hundred camps to govern them.

sentences.zh: 道路降者不絕如流，眾至數十萬。

translations.literal: Surrenders on the roads were unbroken like a flowing stream; the host reached several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendering bands streamed in without pause until his forces numbered several hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 乃命其護軍田茂廣築洛口城，方四十里而居之，密遣房彥藻將兵東略地，取安陸、汝南、淮安、濟陽，河南郡縣多陷於密。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered his Protector of the Army Tian Maoguang to broadly build Luokou City, forty li square, and dwell there; Mi dispatched Fang Yanzao to lead troops east to seize territory, taking Anlu, Runan, Huai'an, and Jiyang; many commanderies and counties of Henan fell to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Protector of the Army Tian Maoguang to build Luokou City on a forty-li square and make it his capital. Li Mi sent Fang Yanzao east with an army to seize Anlu, Runan, Huai'an, and Jiyang, and one Henan commandery and county after another fell into his hands.

sentences.zh: 雁門郡丞河東陳孝意與虎賁郎將王智辯共討劉武周，圍其桑干鎮。

translations.literal: Yanmen commandery assistant Chen Xiaoyi of Hedong and Tiger-Fierce Commandant Wang Zhibian together attacked Liu Wuzhou and besieged his Sanggan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xiaoyi of Hedong, assistant prefect of Yanmen commandery, and Tiger-Fierce Commandant Wang Zhibian jointly marched against Liu Wuzhou and encircled his stronghold at Sanggan.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，武周與突厥合兵擊智辯，殺之；

translations.literal: On renyin, Wuzhou joined forces with the Turks, attacked Zhibian, and killed him;
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day, Wuzhou allied with the Turks to strike Zhibian and slew him;

sentences.zh: 孝意奔還雁門。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi fled back to Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi fled back to Yanmen commandery.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁卯，武周襲破樓煩郡，進取汾陽宮，獲隋宮人，以賂突厥始畢可汗；

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingmao, Wuzhou launched a surprise attack and overran Loufan commandery, advanced to seize Fenyang Palace, captured Sui palace women, and used them to bribe Shibi Khan of the Turks;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingmao, Wuzhou stormed and broke Loufan commandery, pushed toward Fenyang Palace, seized palace women of the Sui court, and sent them as gifts to Shibi Khan of the Turks;

sentences.zh: 始畢以馬報之，兵勢益振，又攻陷定襄。

translations.literal: Shibi responded with horses; his military momentum grew stronger still, and he again captured Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi repaid the gift with horses; Wuzhou's army grew ever bolder, and he went on to take Dingxiang as well.

sentences.zh: 突厥立武周為定楊可汗，遺以狼頭纛。

translations.literal: The Turks established Wuzhou as Khan Dingyang and presented him with a wolf-head banner.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks raised Wuzhou to the title Khan Dingyang and conferred upon him a wolf-head banner.

sentences.zh: 武周即皇帝位，立妻沮氏為皇后，改元天興。

translations.literal: Wuzhou ascended the imperial throne, installed his wife Lady Ju as empress, and changed the era name to Tianxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou proclaimed himself emperor, made his wife, the Lady Ju, empress, and declared a new era named Tianxing.

sentences.zh: 以衛士楊伏念為尚書左僕射，妹婿同縣苑君璋為內史令。

translations.literal: He appointed guard Yang Funian as Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat and his sister's husband, Yuan Junzhang of the same county, as Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He named the guardsman Yang Funian Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat and his brother-in-law Yuan Junzhang of the same county Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武周引兵圍雁門，陳孝意悉力拒守，乘間出擊武周，屢破之；

translations.literal: Wuzhou led troops to besiege Yanmen; Chen Xiaoyi defended with all his strength, seized openings to sortie against Wuzhou, and repeatedly defeated him;
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou brought his army to besiege Yanmen. Chen Xiaoyi held the city with every ounce of strength, and whenever a chance opened he sallied forth against Wuzhou and beat him back again and again;

sentences.zh: 既而外無救援，遣間使詣江都，皆不報。

translations.literal: Before long there was no relief from outside; he sent secret envoys to Jiangdu, but received no response at all.
translations.idiomatic: In time no help came from outside. He dispatched secret emissaries to Jiangdu, yet none of their appeals received any answer.

sentences.zh: 孝意誓以必死。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi swore he would die without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi vowed to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 旦暮向詔敕庫俯伏流涕，悲動左右。

translations.literal: Morning and evening he prostrated himself before the imperial edict archive and wept; his grief moved those around him.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening he bowed before the vault of imperial edicts and wept until the grief moved all who stood near him.

sentences.zh: 圍城百餘日，食盡，校尉張倫殺孝意以降。

translations.literal: The siege lasted more than a hundred days; when provisions were exhausted, Commandant Zhang Lun killed Xiaoyi to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a hundred days under siege the food ran out. Commandant Zhang Lun murdered Xiaoyi and opened the gates in surrender.

sentences.zh: 梁師都略定雕陰、弘化、延安等郡，遂即皇帝位，國號梁，改元永隆。

translations.literal: Liang Shidu pacified the commanderies of Diaoyin, Honghua, Yan'an, and others, then ascended the imperial throne; his state was named Liang, and he changed the era name to Yonglong.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shidu brought Diaoyin, Honghua, Yan'an, and the surrounding commanderies under his control, then proclaimed himself emperor. He named his state Liang and adopted the era name Yonglong.

sentences.zh: 始畢遺以狼頭纛，號為大度毘伽可汗。

translations.literal: Shibi presented him with a wolf-head banner and styled him Khan Dadu Pijia.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi Khan sent him a wolf-head banner and invested him as Khan Dadu Pijia.

sentences.zh: 師都乃引突厥居河南之地，攻破鹽川郡。

translations.literal: Shidu thereupon brought the Turks to settle in the lands south of the Yellow River and stormed and broke Yanchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shidu then settled Turk allies south of the Yellow River and captured Yanchuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 左翊衛蒲城郭子和坐事徙榆林。

translations.literal: Guo Zihe of Pucheng, Left Wing Guard, was banished to Yulin for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zihe of Pucheng, an officer of the Left Wing Guard, was exiled to Yulin on account of a crime.

sentences.zh: 會郡中大饑，子和潛結敢死士十八人攻郡門，執郡丞王才，數以不恤百姓，斬之，開倉賑施。

translations.literal: Just then famine struck the commandery. Zihe secretly rallied eighteen men willing to die for the cause, stormed the commandery gate, seized Assistant Prefect Wang Cai, charged him with neglect of the people, beheaded him, and opened the granaries to distribute relief.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the commandery. Zihe quietly gathered eighteen men ready to die, attacked the gate, seized Assistant Prefect Wang Cai, denounced him for caring nothing for the people, executed him, and opened the storehouses to feed the starving.

sentences.zh: 自稱永樂王，改元丑平。

translations.literal: He styled himself Prince of Yongle and changed the era name to Chouping.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed himself Prince of Yongle and declared the era name Chouping.

sentences.zh: 尊其父為太公，以其弟子政為尚書令，子端、子升為左右僕射。

translations.literal: He honored his father as Grand Duke, appointed his younger brother Zizheng as Director of the Secretariat, and made his sons Ziduan and Zisheng Left and Right Vice Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He ennobled his father as Grand Duke, made his younger brother Zizheng Director of the Secretariat, and appointed his sons Ziduan and Zisheng as the Left and Right Vice Ministers.

sentences.zh: 有二千餘騎，南連梁師都，北附突厥，各遣子為質以自固。

translations.literal: He had more than two thousand horsemen; to the south he linked with Liang Shidu and to the north attached himself to the Turks; each party sent a son as hostage to secure the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: With more than two thousand mounted followers he allied with Liang Shidu in the south and submitted to the Turks in the north; each side sent a son as hostage to bind the pact.

sentences.zh: 始畢以劉武周為定楊天子，梁師都為解事天子，子和為平楊天子；

translations.literal: Shibi made Liu Wuzhou Heaven's Son Dingyang, Liang Shidu Heaven's Son of Practical Affairs, and Zihe Heaven's Son Pingyang;
translations.idiomatic: Shibi Khan titled Liu Wuzhou the Dingyang Son of Heaven, Liang Shidu the Capable Affairs Son of Heaven, and Zihe the Pingyang Son of Heaven;

sentences.zh: 子和固辭不敢當，乃更以為屋利設。

translations.literal: Zihe steadfastly declined, not daring to accept the title, so he was instead made Ulisi.
translations.idiomatic: Zihe repeatedly refused, unwilling to assume such a rank, and was given the Turkic title Ulisi instead.

sentences.zh: 汾陰薛舉，僑居金城，驍勇絕倫，家貲巨萬，交結豪傑，雄於西邊，為金城府校尉。

translations.literal: Xue Ju of Fenyin, living as a resident in Jincheng, was peerless in fierce courage; his household possessed wealth of tens of thousands, he cultivated ties with powerful men, dominated the western frontier, and served as a company commander in the Jincheng prefectural guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju, originally from Fenyin but domiciled at Jincheng, was a warrior without equal. His household commanded enormous wealth, he cultivated the region's boldest men, and his name towered across the western marches. He held a company command in the Jincheng prefectural guard.

sentences.zh: 時隴右盜起，金城令郝瑗募兵得數千人，使舉將而討之。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose in Longyou; Jincheng Magistrate Hao Yuan recruited several thousand troops and put Ju in command to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit armies were rising across Longyou. Magistrate Hao Yuan of Jincheng raised several thousand men and placed Ju at their head to hunt the raiders down.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸未，方授甲，置酒饗士。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on guiwei, just as armor was being issued, he set out wine and feasted the troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on guiwei, as armor was being issued he spread a feast for his men.

sentences.zh: 舉與其子仁果及同黨十三人，於座劫瑗發兵，囚郡縣官，開倉賑施。

translations.literal: Ju, his son Renguo, and thirteen confederates, at the banquet seized Yuan, raised troops, imprisoned the commandery and county officials, and opened the granaries to distribute relief.
translations.idiomatic: At the feast Ju, his son Renguo, and thirteen conspirators seized Yuan, took command of the army, locked up the commandery and county officials, and opened the storehouses to feed the people.

sentences.zh: 自稱西秦霸王，改元秦興。

translations.literal: He styled himself Overlord of Western Qin and changed the era name to Qinxing.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed himself Overlord of Western Qin and declared the era name Qinxing.

sentences.zh: 以仁果為齊公，少子仁越為晉公，招集群盜，掠官牧馬。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Renguo as Duke of Qi, his youngest son Renyue as Duke of Jin, gathered the scattered bandit hosts, and seized government pasture horses.
translations.idiomatic: He made Renguo Duke of Qi and his youngest son Renyue Duke of Jin, rallied the roving bandit bands, and stripped the government stud herds.

sentences.zh: 賊帥宗羅□帥眾歸之，以為義興公。

translations.literal: Bandit chief Zong Luohou led his followers to join him, and Ju made him Duke of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit leader Zong Luohou brought his host to Ju's banner and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 將軍皇甫綰將兵一萬屯枹罕，舉選精銳二千人襲之，遂克枹罕。

translations.literal: General Huangfu Wan commanded ten thousand men encamped at Fuhan; Ju selected two thousand elite troops to raid him and thereupon captured Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: General Huangfu Wan held Fuhan with ten thousand men. Ju picked two thousand picked fighters, struck by surprise, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 岷山羌酋鐘利俗擁眾二萬歸之，舉兵大振。

translations.literal: Zhong Lisu, chieftain of the Minshan Qiang, brought a following of twenty thousand to join him; Ju's army swelled dramatically.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Lisu, chieftain of the Minshan Qiang, rallied twenty thousand men to Ju's cause, and Ju's power surged.

sentences.zh: 更以仁果為齊王，領東道行軍元帥，仁越為晉王，兼河州刺史，羅□為興王，以副仁果；

translations.literal: He again enfeoffed Renguo as King of Qi and made him commander-in-chief on the eastern campaign route; Renyue as King of Jin and concurrently Inspector of He Province; and Luohou as King of Xing to assist Renguo;
translations.idiomatic: He elevated Renguo to King of Qi as commander-in-chief on the eastern front, made Renyue King of Jin and concurrently Inspector of He Province, and appointed Luohou King of Xing to serve under Renguo;

sentences.zh: 分兵略地，取西平、澆河二郡。

translations.literal: He divided his forces to seize territory and captured the two commanderies of Xiping and Jiaohe.
translations.idiomatic: He sent columns to expand his holdings and took the commanderies of Xiping and Jiaohe.

sentences.zh: 未幾，盡有隴西之地，眾至十三萬。

translations.literal: Before long he possessed the whole of Longxi; his host reached one hundred thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In short order he held all of Longxi, and his forces swelled to one hundred thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 李密以孟讓為總管、齊郡公，己丑夜，讓帥步騎二千入東都外郭，燒掠豐都市，比曉而去。

translations.literal: Li Mi appointed Meng Rang as overseer-general and Duke of Qi Commandery. On the night of jichou, Rang led two thousand infantry and cavalry into the outer ward of the Eastern Capital, burned and plundered Fengdu Market, and withdrew before dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi made Meng Rang overseer-general and Duke of Qi Commandery. On the jichou night Rang led two thousand horse and foot into the outer city of the Eastern Capital, burned and sacked Fengdu Market, and withdrew before daybreak.

sentences.zh: 於是東京居民悉遷入宮城，台省府寺皆滿。

translations.literal: Thereupon all residents of the Eastern Capital moved inside the palace city; the bureaus, ministries, and offices were all filled to capacity.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the Eastern Capital were driven into the palace city until the halls of government were packed tight.

sentences.zh: 鞏縣長柴孝和、監察御史鄭頲以城降密，密以孝和為護軍，頲為右長史。

translations.literal: Chai Xiaohe, magistrate of Gong County, and Supervising Censor Zheng Ting surrendered the city to Mi; Mi made Xiaohe Protector of the Army and Ting Right Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Gong County Magistrate Chai Xiaohe and Supervising Censor Zheng Ting handed over their city to Mi, who named Xiaohe Protector of the Army and Ting Right Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 裴仁基每破賊，得軍資，悉以賞士卒，監軍御史蕭懷靜不許，士卒怨之；

translations.literal: Whenever Pei Renji defeated bandits and obtained military supplies, he gave them all as rewards to his soldiers; Supervising Censor Xiao Huaijing forbade this, and the troops resented him;
translations.idiomatic: Every time Pei Renji routed the rebels and seized supplies he paid them out to his men. Army Supervising Censor Xiao Huaijing forbade it, and the soldiers turned against him;

sentences.zh: 懷靜又屢求仁基長短，劾奏之。

translations.literal: Huaijing also repeatedly sought out Renji's faults and impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaijing kept hunting for grounds to attack Renji and filed impeachments against him.

sentences.zh: 倉城之戰，仁基失期不至，聞劉長恭等敗，懼不敢進，屯百花谷，固壘自守，又鞏獲罪於朝。

translations.literal: In the battle at Cangcheng Renji failed to arrive on schedule; hearing that Liu Changgong and others had been defeated, he was afraid to advance, encamped at Baihua Valley, held fast behind strong fortifications, and was again found guilty at court.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Cangcheng Renji missed his rendezvous. Learning that Liu Changgong's force had been broken, he dared not push forward, dug in at Baihua Valley, and drew fresh condemnation from the court.

sentences.zh: 李密知其狼狽，使人說之，啖以厚利。

translations.literal: Li Mi knew his disarray and sent men to win him over, tempting him with great rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi saw how cornered Renji had become and sent envoys to woo him with lavish promises.

sentences.zh: 賈務本之子閏甫在軍中，勸仁基降密，仁基曰：「如蕭御史何？」

translations.literal: Runfu, son of Jia Wuben, was in the army and urged Renji to surrender to Mi. Renji said, "What of Supervising Censor Xiao?"
translations.idiomatic: Jia Wuben's son Runfu served in Renji's camp and urged him to defect to Mi. Renji asked, "And what of Supervising Censor Xiao?"

sentences.zh: 閏甫曰：「蕭君如棲上雞，若不知機變，在明公一刀耳。」

translations.literal: Runfu said, "Master Xiao is like a roosting hen; if he does not know when to adapt, one stroke of your blade will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Runfu answered, "Xiao is no more than a hen on a perch. If he cannot read the moment, you need only one stroke of the blade, my lord."

sentences.zh: 仁基從之，遣閏甫詣密請降。

translations.literal: Renji agreed and dispatched Runfu to Mi to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Renji accepted the counsel and sent Runfu to Mi to offer submission.

sentences.zh: 密大喜，以閏甫為元帥府司兵參軍，兼直記室事，使之覆命，遺仁基書，慰納之，仁基還屯虎牢。

translations.literal: Mi was greatly pleased; he made Runfu a staff officer in charge of military affairs at the marshal's headquarters and concurrently responsible for secretarial duties, sent him back with the reply, wrote Renji a letter of welcome and acceptance, and Renji returned to encamp at Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was elated. He made Runfu a military affairs officer on his marshal's staff with secretarial duties, sent him back with his answer, and wrote Renji a letter of welcome. Renji withdrew to camp at Hulao.

sentences.zh: 蕭懷靜密表其事，仁基知之，遂殺懷靜，帥其眾以虎牢降密。

translations.literal: Xiao Huaijing secretly memorialized the court about this; when Renji learned of it he killed Huaijing, led his troops from Hulao, and surrendered to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Huaijing filed a secret report to the throne. Renji found out, executed him on the spot, and led his army from Hulao over to Mi.

sentences.zh: 密以仁基為上柱國、河東公；

translations.literal: Mi made Renji Grand Pillar of State and Duke of Hedong;
translations.idiomatic: Mi ennobled Renji as Grand Pillar of State and Duke of Hedong;

sentences.zh: 仁基子行儼，驍勇善戰，密亦以為上柱國、絳郡公。

translations.literal: Renji's son Xingyan was fierce and skilled in battle; Mi also made him Grand Pillar of State and Duke of Jiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Renji's son Xingyan was a bold and capable fighter, and Mi gave him the same rank of Grand Pillar of State and the title Duke of Jiang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 密得秦叔寶及東阿程咬金，皆用為驃騎。

translations.literal: Mi obtained Qin Shubao and Cheng Yaojin of Dong'e and appointed both as marshals of swift cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Mi recruited Qin Shubao and Cheng Yaojin of Dong'e and made both marshals of the swift-cavalry corps.

sentences.zh: 選軍中尤驍勇者八千人，分隸四驃騎以自衛，號曰內軍，常曰：「此八千人足當百萬。」

translations.literal: He selected eight thousand of the fiercest warriors in the army, assigned them to the four swift-cavalry marshals as a personal guard, and called them the Inner Army, often saying, "These eight thousand are fully equal to a million."
translations.idiomatic: From his ranks he picked eight thousand of the boldest fighters, divided them among four swift-cavalry marshals as his personal guard, and named them the Inner Army. He was fond of saying, "Eight thousand such men are worth a million on any field."

sentences.zh: 咬金後更名知節。

translations.literal: Yaojin later changed his name to Zhijie.
translations.idiomatic: Yaojin later took the name Zhijie.

sentences.zh: 羅士信、趙仁基皆帥眾歸密，密署為總管，使各統所部。

translations.literal: Luo Shixin and Zhao Renji both led their followers to join Mi; Mi appointed them overseer-generals and had each command his own force.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shixin and Zhao Renji both brought their bands to Mi's camp. He made them overseer-generals, each commanding his own troops.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，密遣裴仁基、孟讓帥二萬餘人襲回洛東倉，破之；

translations.literal: On guisi, Mi dispatched Pei Renji and Meng Rang with more than twenty thousand men to raid Huiluo East Granary and broke it;
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Mi sent Pei Renji and Meng Rang with more than twenty thousand men against Huiluo East Granary and carried the place;

sentences.zh: 遂燒天津橋，縱兵大掠。

translations.literal: They then burned Tianjin Bridge and let the troops loot on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: They torched Tianjin Bridge and unleashed their men in a sweeping rampage.

sentences.zh: 東都出兵擊之，仁基等敗走，密自帥眾屯回洛倉。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital sent troops to strike them; Renji and the others were routed and fled; Mi personally led his host to encamp at Huiluo Granary.
translations.idiomatic: Forces from the Eastern Capital marched out against them; Renji's column was beaten back; and Mi himself moved up to hold Huiluo Granary.

sentences.zh: 東都兵尚二十餘萬人，乘城擊柝，晝夜不解甲。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital still had more than two hundred thousand troops; they manned the walls and sounded the night watches, day and night never doffing their armor.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital still fielded more than two hundred thousand men who manned the battlements, beat the night watches, and never laid down their armor.

sentences.zh: 密攻偃師、金墉，皆不克；

translations.literal: Mi attacked Yanshi and Jin Yong and could not capture either;
translations.idiomatic: Mi assaulted Yanshi and Jin Yong but failed to take either city;

sentences.zh: 乙未，還洛口。

translations.literal: On yimwei, he returned to Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: On yimwei he withdrew to Luokou.

sentences.zh: 東都城內乏糧，而布帛山積，至以絹為汲綆，然布以爨。

translations.literal: Inside the Eastern Capital food was scarce, yet silk and cloth piled like mountains; people even used silk as rope for drawing water and burned cloth for cooking fuel.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the Eastern Capital grain ran dry while silk and cloth lay heaped like hills—so people braided silk into water buckets and burned cloth to cook their meals.

sentences.zh: 越王侗使人運回洛倉米入城，遣兵五千屯豐都市，五千屯上春門，五千屯北邙山，為九營，首尾相應，以備密。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Yang Tong sent men to transport grain from Huiluo Granary into the city, dispatched five thousand troops to garrison Fengdu Market, five thousand to Upper Spring Gate, five thousand to Mount Beimang, forming nine camps that linked head to tail in mutual support to guard against Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yang Tong of Yue had grain trucked in from Huiluo Granary and posted five thousand men at Fengdu Market, five thousand at Upper Spring Gate, and five thousand on Mount Beimang—nine linked camps in all—to block Mi's advance.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，房獻伯陷汝陰，淮陽太守趙阤舉郡降密。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Fang Xianbo captured Runan; Huaiyang Administrator Zhao Tuo surrendered the whole commandery to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Fang Xianbo took Runan, and Huaiyang Prefect Zhao Tuo handed over his entire jurisdiction to Mi.

sentences.zh: 己亥，密帥眾三萬復據回洛倉，大修營塹以逼東都；

translations.literal: On jihai, Mi led thirty thousand men to reoccupy Huiluo Granary, built fortifications on a grand scale to press the Eastern Capital;
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Mi returned with thirty thousand men to Huiluo Granary and dug extensive entrenchments to choke the Eastern Capital;

sentences.zh: 段達等出兵七萬拒之。

translations.literal: Duan Da and others led seventy thousand troops to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da marched out with seventy thousand men to meet him.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，戰於倉北，隋兵敗走。

translations.literal: On xinchou, they fought north of the granary; Sui troops were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou the two sides clashed north of the granary, and the Sui army broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 丁未，密使其幕府移檄郡縣，數煬帝十罪，且曰：「罄南山之竹，書罪無窮；

translations.literal: On dingwei, Mi had his staff issue a proclamation to the commanderies and counties, enumerating ten crimes of Emperor Yang, and saying, "Exhaust the bamboo of the Southern Mountains and still the catalogue of crimes would never end;
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Mi's staff circulated a manifesto across the commanderies and counties, listing ten crimes of Emperor Yang. It declared, "Strip the Southern Mountains bare of bamboo and you could still never finish writing his offenses;

sentences.zh: 決東海之波，流惡難盡。」

translations.literal: Empty the waves of the Eastern Sea and still the flood of evil would be hard to exhaust."
translations.idiomatic: Drain the Eastern Sea and still his torrent of wickedness could not be spent."

sentences.zh: 祖君彥之辭也。

translations.literal: These were the words of Zu Junyan.
translations.idiomatic: The prose was Zu Junyan's.

sentences.zh: 趙王侗遣太常丞元善達間行賊中，詣江都奏稱：「李密有眾百萬，圍逼東都，據洛口倉，城內無食。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Yang Tong dispatched Palace Minister of Ceremonies Assistant Yuan Shanda by secret route through the bandit zone to report at Jiangdu, saying, "Li Mi has a host of a million men, is besieging the Eastern Capital, holds Luokou Granary, and there is no food within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yang Tong of Zhao sent Palace Minister of Ceremonies Assistant Yuan Shanda by a hidden path through rebel-held territory to reach Jiangdu and report: "Li Mi commands a million men, has the Eastern Capital under siege, holds Luokou Granary, and the city has no grain left.

sentences.zh: 若陛下速還，烏合必散；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty returns quickly, this mob will surely disperse;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty returns at once this rabble will scatter;

sentences.zh: 不然者，東都決沒。」

translations.literal: Otherwise the Eastern Capital will certainly fall."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the Eastern Capital is doomed."

sentences.zh: 因歔欷嗚咽，帝為之改容。

translations.literal: He then sobbed and wept convulsively, and the emperor's expression changed on his account.
translations.idiomatic: He broke into sobs, and even the emperor's face changed.

sentences.zh: 虞世基進曰：「越王年少，此輩誑之。

translations.literal: Yu Shiqi stepped forward and said, "The Prince of Yue is young; these people deceived him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shiqi spoke up: "The Prince of Yue is still young. These men fed him lies.

sentences.zh: 若如所言，善達何緣來至！」

translations.literal: If things were as he says, how could Shanda possibly have gotten here!"
translations.idiomatic: If any of that were true, how could Shanda ever have reached us!"

sentences.zh: 帝乃勃然怒曰：「善達小人，敢廷辱我！」

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon erupted in anger and said, "Shanda is a base fellow who dares insult me in open court!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flared with rage. "Shanda is a wretch who dares humiliate me before the whole court!"

sentences.zh: 因使經賊中向東陽催運，善達遂為群盜所殺。

translations.literal: He therefore sent him back through the bandit zone to hasten transport at Dongyang, and Shanda was thereupon killed by the bandit hosts.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Shanda sent back through rebel country to expedite the Dongyang grain convoy, and bandits cut him down on the road.

sentences.zh: 是後人人杜口，莫敢以賊聞。

translations.literal: After this everyone sealed his lips; no one dared to mention bandits to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: After that no one at court dared breathe a word about the rebels.

sentences.zh: 世基容貌沉審，言多合意，特為帝所親愛，朝臣無與為比；

translations.literal: Shiqi's bearing was grave and steady; his words mostly suited the emperor's mind; he was especially cherished by the emperor, and no court official could compare with him;
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi carried himself with grave composure, and his words almost always struck the emperor's mood. No minister enjoyed such favor;

sentences.zh: 親黨憑之，鬻官賣獄，賄賂公行，其門如市。

translations.literal: Relatives and partisans relied on him to sell offices and justice; bribes were openly traded, and his gate was like a market.
translations.idiomatic: His kin and clients traded offices and verdicts for cash. Bribes changed hands in the open, and petitioners crowded his gate like a market square.

sentences.zh: 由是朝野共疾怨之。

translations.literal: Therefore court and commoners alike hated and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike came to loathe him.

sentences.zh: 內史舍人封德彝托附世基，以世基不閒吏務，密為指畫，宣行詔命，諂順帝意。

translations.literal: Secretariat Attendant-in-Ordinary Feng Deyi attached himself to Shiqi; since Shiqi was unfamiliar with administrative affairs, Deyi secretly drafted plans, promulgated edicts, and flattered the emperor's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat attendant Feng Deyi clung to Shiqi's coattails. Shiqi knew little of routine administration, so Deyi drafted the orders behind the scenes, issued the edicts, and shaped every word to please the throne.

sentences.zh: 群臣表疏忤旨者，皆屏而不奏。

translations.literal: Memorials from the ministers that ran counter to the emperor's intent were all suppressed and not presented.
translations.idiomatic: Any memorial that crossed the emperor's mood was buried and never reached his desk.

sentences.zh: 鞫獄用法，多峻文深詆，論功行賞，則抑削就薄。

translations.literal: In judging cases the law was applied with harsh statutes and deep denunciation; in discussing merit and granting rewards, rewards were cut down and kept thin.
translations.idiomatic: In criminal cases the statutes were stretched to their harshest reading; when honors were due, the grants were pared to the bone.

sentences.zh: 故世基之寵日隆而隋政益壞，皆德彝所為也。

translations.literal: Thus while Shiqi's favor grew daily, Sui governance worsened further still—and all of it was Deyi's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi's star rose even as the Sui order rotted further—and the rot was largely Deyi's work.

sentences.zh: 初，唐公李淵娶於神武肅公竇毅，生四男，建成、世民、玄霸、元吉；

translations.literal: Earlier, Duke of Tang Li Yuan had married the daughter of Shenwu Su Duke Dou Yi and fathered four sons: Jiancheng, Shimin, Xuanba, and Yuanji;
translations.idiomatic: In earlier days Duke Li Yuan of Tang had married a daughter of Duke Dou Yi of Shenwu Su and fathered four sons: Jiancheng, Shimin, Xuanba, and Yuanji;

sentences.zh: 一女，適太子千牛備身臨汾柴紹。

translations.literal: One daughter, who married Chai Shao of Linfen, Gentleman-at-Arms for the Heir Apparent's Thousand Oxen Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He also had a daughter, who wed Chai Shao of Linfen, a gentleman-at-arms in the Heir Apparent's Thousand Oxen Guard.

sentences.zh: 世民聰明勇決，識量過人，見隋室方亂，陰有安天下之志，傾身下士，散財結客，鹹得其歡心。

translations.literal: Shimin was intelligent, brave, and resolute; his discernment and capacity surpassed other men. Seeing the Sui house in turmoil, he secretly harbored the ambition to bring peace to the realm; he humbled himself before scholars, distributed wealth to cultivate clients, and all won his warm regard.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin was bright, bold, and far-seeing. With the Sui house coming apart he quietly nursed the ambition to reorder the realm. He sought out men of talent, spent freely to gather allies, and won the hearts of all who crossed his path.

sentences.zh: 世民娶右驍衛將軍長孫晟之女；

translations.literal: Shimin married the daughter of Right Swift-Cavalry Guard General Zhangsun Sheng;
translations.idiomatic: Shimin had taken as his wife the daughter of Zhangsun Sheng, general of the Right Swift-Cavalry Guard;

sentences.zh: 右勳衛長孫順德，晟之族弟也，與右勳侍池陽劉弘基，皆避遼東之役，亡命在晉陽，依淵，與世民善。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Shunde of the Right Meritorious Guard, a clansman of Sheng, and Liu Hongji of Chiyang, Right Meritorious Attendant, had both fled to avoid the Liaodong campaign and were living as fugitives at Jinyang under Yuan's patronage; both were on good terms with Shimin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Shunde of the Right Meritorious Guard—a clansman of Sheng's—and Liu Hongji of Chiyang, a Right Meritorious Attendant, had both slipped away rather than march to Liaodong. They were sheltering at Jinyang under Yuan's protection and had grown close to Shimin.

sentences.zh: 左親衛竇琮，熾之孫也，亦亡命在太原，素與世民有隙，每以自疑；

translations.literal: Dou Cong of the Left Personal Guard, grandson of Chi, was also living as a fugitive at Taiyuan; he had long been at odds with Shimin and constantly doubted himself;
translations.idiomatic: Dou Cong of the Left Personal Guard, grandson of Dou Chi, was likewise hiding out at Taiyuan. He and Shimin had old grievances, and Cong lived in constant fear;

sentences.zh: 世民加意待之，出入臥內，琮意乃安。

translations.literal: Shimin treated him with special care, admitting him freely into his private quarters, and Cong's mind was thereupon set at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin went out of his way to honor him, welcomed him into his inner rooms, and Cong's fears subsided.

sentences.zh: 晉陽宮監猗氏裴寂，晉陽令武功劉文靜，相與同宿，見城上烽火，寂歎曰：「貧賤如此，復逢亂離，將何以自存！」

translations.literal: Pei Ji of Yishi, intendant of Jinyang Palace, and Liu Wenjing of Wugong, magistrate of Jinyang, were lodging together. Seeing beacon fires on the city wall, Ji sighed and said, "Poor and lowly as we are, and now meeting this age of turmoil—how shall we preserve ourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji of Yishi, keeper of Jinyang Palace, and Liu Wenjing of Wugong, magistrate of Jinyang, were sharing quarters when they saw beacon fires atop the wall. Ji sighed, "We are poor men already, and now the world is tearing itself apart. How are we to survive?"

sentences.zh: 文靜笑曰：「時事可知，吾二人相得，何憂貧賤！」

translations.literal: Wenjing laughed and said, "The times can be read; if the two of us find each other, why worry over poverty and low status!"
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing laughed. "The times tell their own story. With the two of us together, why fret over being poor?"

sentences.zh: 文靜見李世民而異之，深自結納，謂寂曰：「此非常人，豁達類漢高，神武同魏祖，年雖少，命世才也。」

translations.literal: Wenjing met Li Shimin and marked him as extraordinary; he drew close to him in earnest and said to Ji, "This is no ordinary man—open-handed like Han Gaozu, martial and divine like Wei Wudi; though young, he is a talent fated to command an age."
translations.idiomatic: When Wenjing met Li Shimin he knew at once that the young man was no ordinary soul. He attached himself closely and told Ji, "This is a man apart—magnanimous as Emperor Gaozu of Han, fierce and shrewd as Emperor Wu of Wei. Young as he is, he has the makings of a world-conqueror."

sentences.zh: 寂初未然之。

translations.literal: Ji at first did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was not persuaded at first.

sentences.zh: 文靜坐與李密連昏，系太原獄，世民就省之。

translations.literal: Wenjing, convicted for marriage ties with Li Mi, was imprisoned at Taiyuan; Shimin went to visit him in custody.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing had been jailed at Taiyuan for maintaining marriage ties with Li Mi. Shimin visited him in prison.

sentences.zh: 文靜曰：「天下大亂，非高、光之才，不能定也。」

translations.literal: Wenjing said, "The realm is in great chaos; without the talent of a Gaozu or Guangwu, it cannot be settled."
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing said, "The empire is drowning in chaos. Only someone with the stature of a Gaozu or a Guangwu can set it right."

sentences.zh: 世民曰：「安知其無，但人不識耳。

translations.literal: Shimin said, "How do you know such men do not exist? It is only that people do not recognize them.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin replied, "Who is to say they are not out there? The trouble is that no one recognizes them.

sentences.zh: 我來相省，非兒女子之情，欲與君議大事也。

translations.literal: I came to visit you not from the sentiments of women and children, but because I wish to discuss great affairs with you.
translations.idiomatic: I came to see you not out of idle friendship but to speak of weightier matters.

sentences.zh: 計將安出？」

translations.literal: What plan do you propose?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you propose we do?"

sentences.zh: 文靜曰：「今主上南巡江、淮，李密圍逼東都，群盜殆以萬數。

translations.literal: Wenjing said, "Now the sovereign is touring south through the Jiang and Huai regions; Li Mi is pressing the Eastern Capital in siege; bandit hosts number nearly in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing went on, "The emperor is on a southern progress through the Yangtze and Huai lands. Li Mi has the Eastern Capital under siege. The rebel bands must number in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 當此之際，有真主驅駕而用之，取天下如反掌耳。

translations.literal: At a moment such as this, were there a true lord to drive the chariot and put him to use, taking the realm would be like turning the palm.
translations.idiomatic: In such a moment, if a true sovereign could be found and put in the saddle, winning the empire would be as easy as turning over one's hand.

sentences.zh: 太原百姓皆避盜入城，文靜為令數年，知其豪傑，一旦收集，可得十萬人，尊公所將之兵復且數萬，一言出口，誰敢不從！

translations.literal: All the common people of Taiyuan have fled from bandits into the city; Wenjing has been magistrate for several years and knows its powerful men; if gathered at once, one could obtain a hundred thousand men, and the troops led by Your Lordship number again several ten thousands—a word spoken, who would dare not follow!
translations.idiomatic: Every commoner in Taiyuan has taken refuge inside the walls from the bandits. I have been magistrate here for years and know the local leaders. Summon them now and you can raise a hundred thousand men. Your own command already counts tens of thousands besides. Once the word is spoken, who would refuse to follow?

sentences.zh: 以此乘虛入關，號令天下，不過半年，帝業成矣。」

translations.literal: With this force, seizing the vacant pass into the heartland and issuing commands to the realm—in no more than half a year imperial founding would be accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: Strike through the pass while the realm lies open, proclaim your rule to all under heaven, and within half a year the throne would be yours."

sentences.zh: 世民笑曰：「君言正合我意。」

translations.literal: Shimin smiled and said, "Your words exactly match my thought."
translations.idiomatic: Shimin smiled. "You have spoken my own mind."

sentences.zh: 乃陰部署賓客，淵不之知也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he secretly arranged his clients; Yuan did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: He then began secretly to deploy his followers. Yuan knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 世民恐淵不從，猶豫久之，不敢言。

translations.literal: Shimin feared Yuan would not consent and hesitated a long while, not daring to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin feared Yuan would refuse and long held his tongue, unable to bring himself to speak.

sentences.zh: 淵與裴寂有舊，每相與宴語，或連日夜。

translations.literal: Yuan and Pei Ji had old ties; they would feast and converse together, sometimes for days and nights on end.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and Pei Ji were old acquaintances and often feasted and talked together, sometimes for days and nights without break.

sentences.zh: 文靜欲因寂關說，乃引寂與世民交。

translations.literal: Wenjing wished to approach and persuade through Ji, and so introduced Ji to Shimin to become acquainted.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing meant to reach Yuan through Ji and so brought Ji and Shimin together.

sentences.zh: 世民出私錢數百萬，使龍山令高斌廉與寂博，稍以輸之，寂大喜，由是日從世民游，情款益狎。

translations.literal: Shimin put out several million in private funds, had Longshan Magistrate Gao Binkian gamble with Ji, and gradually lost to him; Ji was greatly pleased, and from this day accompanied Shimin in his outings, their intimacy growing ever closer.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin spent millions of his own money, set Longshan magistrate Gao Binkian to gamble with Ji, and arranged for Gao to lose steadily. Ji was delighted and from then on spent his days in Shimin's company, growing ever more familiar with him.

sentences.zh: 世民乃以其謀告之，寂許諾。

translations.literal: Shimin then told him the plan, and Ji promised his assent.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin confided the plot to him, and Ji agreed.

sentences.zh: 會突厥寇馬邑，淵遣高君雅將兵與馬邑太守王仁恭並力拒之；

translations.literal: It happened that the Turks raided Mayi; Yuan sent Gao Junya to lead troops and, together with Mayi Prefect Wang Rengong, resist them with combined strength;
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided Mayi, Yuan sent Gao Junya with troops to join Mayi prefect Wang Rengong in the defense;

sentences.zh: 仁恭、君雅戰不利，淵恐並獲罪，甚憂之。

translations.literal: Rengong and Junya fought without success; Yuan feared both would be punished together and was deeply worried.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong and Junya were defeated, and Yuan feared they would both be held to account. He was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 世民乘間屏人說淵曰：「今主上無道，百姓困窮，晉陽城外皆為戰場。

translations.literal: Shimin seized an interval, dismissed attendants, and said to Yuan, "Now the sovereign is without the Way; the common people are impoverished and destitute; beyond the walls of Jinyang all has become a battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin found a private moment, dismissed the others, and said to Yuan, "The emperor has lost the Way. The people are starving. Beyond Jinyang's walls, the whole country is a battlefield.

sentences.zh: 大人若守小節，下有寇盜，上有嚴刑，危亡無日。

translations.literal: If my lord clings to petty integrity, with bandits below and harsh penalties above, destruction is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: If you cling to small scruples while bandits ravage below and the court's punishments hang over you, ruin will come any day.

sentences.zh: 不若順民心，興義兵，轉禍為福，此天授之時也。」

translations.literal: Better to follow the people's hearts, raise righteous troops, turn calamity into blessing—this is the time Heaven has granted."
translations.idiomatic: Better to follow the people's will, raise a righteous army, and turn disaster into deliverance. Heaven has given you this hour."

sentences.zh: 淵大驚曰：「汝安得為此言，吾今執汝以告縣官！」

translations.literal: Yuan was greatly alarmed and said, "How dare you speak such words? I shall now seize you and report you to the district officials!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was aghast. "How can you say such a thing? I will arrest you and turn you in to the authorities!"

sentences.zh: 因取紙筆，欲為表。

translations.literal: He then took paper and brush, intending to draft a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He took up brush and paper to write a report.

sentences.zh: 世民徐曰：「世民觀天時人事如此，故敢發言；

translations.literal: Shimin said calmly, "Shimin has observed heaven's seasons and human affairs to be thus, and therefore dared to speak;
translations.idiomatic: Shimin said evenly, "I have watched the times and seen how matters stand. That is why I dared speak.

sentences.zh: 必欲執告，不敢辭死！」

translations.literal: If you must seize and report me, I do not dare refuse death!"
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to arrest me and inform on me, I will not shrink from death."

sentences.zh: 淵曰：「吾豈忍告汝，汝慎勿出口！」

translations.literal: Yuan said, "How could I bear to report you? Be careful not to let such words leave your mouth!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said, "I could never bring myself to inform on you. Not another word of this, mind you!"

sentences.zh: 明日，世民復說淵曰：「今盜賊日繁，遍於天下，大人受詔討賊，賊可盡乎？

translations.literal: The next day Shimin again urged Yuan, saying, "Now bandits grow daily, spread throughout the realm; my lord has received an edict to suppress bandits—can the bandits be exhausted?
translations.idiomatic: The next day Shimin pressed him again. "Banditry grows every day and has spread across the empire. You have been ordered to suppress them. Can you exterminate them all?

sentences.zh: 要之，終不免罪。

translations.literal: In the end, guilt cannot be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: One way or another, you will not escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 且世人皆傳李氏當應圖讖，故李金才無罪，一朝族滅。

translations.literal: Moreover all the world says the Li clan should fulfill the charts and prophecies; therefore Li Jincai, though guiltless, in one morning suffered the extermination of his clan.
translations.idiomatic: And everyone says the Li clan is destined to fulfill the prophecies. Li Jincai was innocent, yet his whole house was wiped out in a single day.

sentences.zh: 大人設能盡賊，則功高不賞，身益危矣！

translations.literal: If my lord could actually exterminate the bandits, then merit too high goes unrewarded, and the person grows ever more imperiled!
translations.idiomatic: Even if you did destroy every bandit, your merit would go unrewarded and your own position would only grow more perilous!

sentences.zh: 唯昨日之言，可以救禍，此萬全之策也，願大人勿疑！」

translations.literal: Only yesterday's words can avert calamity; this is a plan of complete security—may my lord not doubt!"
translations.idiomatic: Only what I said yesterday can save us. It is the surest course. I beg you not to hesitate!"

sentences.zh: 淵乃歎曰：「吾一夕思汝言，亦大有理。

translations.literal: Yuan sighed and said, "I thought upon your words through one night, and they too have great reason.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan sighed. "I spent the night weighing your words. They make a great deal of sense.

sentences.zh: 今日破家亡軀亦由汝，化家為國亦由汝矣！」

translations.literal: Today whether this house is destroyed and bodies perish is also because of you; whether the house is transformed into a state is also because of you!"
translations.idiomatic: Whether this house is ruined or remade as a realm—it will all be because of you!"

sentences.zh: 先是，裴寂私以晉陽宮人侍淵，淵從寂飲，酒酣，寂從容言曰：「二郎陰養士馬，欲舉大事，正為寂以宮人侍公，恐事覺並誅，為此急計耳。

translations.literal: Before this, Pei Ji had privately presented a Jinyang palace woman to serve Yuan; Yuan was drinking with Ji, and when the wine had taken effect Ji said at his ease, "The Second Lord secretly keeps soldiers and horses, intending to raise a great undertaking; it is precisely because Ji presented a palace woman to serve you, fearing that if the matter were discovered we would all be executed together—for this he has pressed so urgent a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Pei Ji had secretly sent a palace woman from Jinyang to attend Yuan. As they drank together and the wine warmed them, Ji said calmly, "Your second son has been gathering men and horses in secret, planning to strike. He is in haste because I gave you that palace woman—if the affair were exposed we would all be put to death together. That is why he is pressing so hard.

sentences.zh: 眾情己協，公意如何？」

translations.literal: The multitude's hearts are already aligned—what is your lordship's thought?"
translations.idiomatic: All parties are already agreed. What do you say?"

sentences.zh: 淵曰：「吾兒誠有此謀，事已如此，當復奈何，正須從之耳。」

translations.literal: Yuan said, "My son truly has this design; affairs have come to such a pass—what can be done but follow it."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said, "My son truly means to do this. Matters have gone so far that there is nothing for it but to go along."

sentences.zh: 帝以淵與王仁恭不能禦寇，遣使者執詣江都。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yuan and Wang Rengong could not repel the raiders, sent an envoy to seize them and convey them to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuan and Wang Rengong had failed to hold off the raiders, the emperor sent envoys to arrest them and bring them to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 淵大懼。

translations.literal: Yuan was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was terrified.

sentences.zh: 世民與寂等復說淵曰：「今主昏國亂，盡忠無益。

translations.literal: Shimin and Ji and the others again urged Yuan, saying, "Now the sovereign is benighted and the state in chaos; exhausting loyalty is of no use.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin, Ji, and the others pressed him again. "The ruler is lost and the realm in chaos. Loyalty will do you no good.

sentences.zh: 偏裨失律，而罪及明公。

translations.literal: Subordinate officers lost discipline, yet guilt reaches the eminent lord.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates break the rules, yet the blame falls on you.

sentences.zh: 事已迫矣，宜早定計。

translations.literal: Affairs are already pressing; you should settle the plan early.
translations.idiomatic: Time is short. You must decide quickly.

sentences.zh: 且晉陽士馬精強，宮監蓄積巨萬，以茲舉事，何患無成！

translations.literal: Moreover Jinyang's soldiers and horses are elite and strong; the palace intendant's stored wealth runs to vast tens of thousands—with this to raise the undertaking, why worry that success will not come!
translations.idiomatic: Jinyang's soldiers and horses are first-rate, and the palace stores hold fortunes beyond counting. With such resources, how could we fail?

sentences.zh: 代王幼沖，關中豪傑並起，未知所附，公若鼓行而西，撫而有之，如探囊中之物耳。

translations.literal: The Prince of Dai is young and tender; heroes of the Guanzhong region are rising together, not yet knowing whom to follow; if your lordship beats the drums and marches west, pacifying and possessing them, it would be like taking something from inside a bag.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Dai is still a child. The strong men of Guanzhong are rising on every side and do not yet know whom to follow. If you march west at once and win them over, taking the region will be like reaching into a sack.

sentences.zh: 奈何受單使之囚，坐取夷滅乎！」

translations.literal: How can one accept the imprisonment of a lone envoy and sit by while extermination is taken!"
translations.idiomatic: Why submit to arrest by a single courier and wait to be wiped out?"

sentences.zh: 淵然之，密部勒，將發；

translations.literal: Yuan assented to this, secretly made dispositions, and was about to set out;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan agreed, made secret preparations, and was ready to move;

sentences.zh: 會帝繼遣使者馳驛赦淵及仁恭，使復舊任，淵謀亦緩。

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor again sent an envoy post-haste to pardon Yuan and Rengong and restore them to their former posts; Yuan's plot likewise slackened.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor soon sent another courier by fast post to pardon Yuan and Rengong and restore them to office, and Yuan's plans eased off.

sentences.zh: 淵之為河東討捕使也，請大理司直夏侯端為副。

translations.literal: When Yuan served as Hedong Pursuit-and-Capture Commissioner, he requested Grand Court of Judicature Direct Clerk Xiahou Duan as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan was appointed Hedong pursuit commissioner, he asked for Xiahou Duan, direct clerk of the Grand Court of Judicature, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 端，詳之孫也，善占候及相人，謂淵曰：「今玉床搖動，帝座不安，參墟得歲，必有真人起於其分，非公而誰乎！

translations.literal: Duan, grandson of Xiang, was skilled at observing signs and reading faces; he said to Yuan, "Now the jade couch shakes, the throne-seat is unsettled; Canqiu receives the year's star—certainly a true lord will rise in that quarter; if not you, then who!
translations.idiomatic: Duan, grandson of Xiahou Xiang, was adept at reading omens and men's faces. He told Yuan, "The throne trembles and the celestial seat is unsettled. Canqiu holds the year's influence—a true sovereign will rise in that direction. If not you, who else?

sentences.zh: 主上猜忍，尤忌諸李，金才既死，公不思變通，必為之次矣。」

translations.literal: The sovereign is suspicious and cruel, especially jealous of all the Li; Jincai is already dead—if your lordship does not consider flexibility, you will surely be next."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is mistrustful and cruel and especially hates the Li clan. Jincai is already dead. If you do not change course, you will be next."

sentences.zh: 淵心然之。

translations.literal: Yuan inwardly assented to this.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was convinced.

sentences.zh: 乃留守晉陽，鷹揚府司馬太原許世緒說淵曰：「公姓在圖菉，名應歌謠；

translations.literal: When he remained to garrison Jinyang, Xushi of Taiyuan, Eagle-Raising Prefecture adjutant, urged Yuan, saying, "Your lordship's surname is in the charts and registers, your name answers the folk songs;
translations.idiomatic: While he held Jinyang, Xushi of Taiyuan, adjutant of the Eagle-Raising Prefecture, urged Yuan, "Your surname is written in the prophecies and your name in the ballads;

sentences.zh: 據五郡之兵，當四戰之地，舉事則帝業可成，端居則亡不旋踵；

translations.literal: Holding the soldiers of five commanderies, standing in a land of battle on four sides—raise the undertaking and imperial founding can be achieved; sit still and destruction will not wait for the turning of the heel;
translations.idiomatic: you command the armies of five commanderies from a crossroads of war. Rise now and an empire can be yours. Sit idle and you will not outlive the moment.

sentences.zh: 唯公圖之。」

translations.literal: Only may your lordship consider it."
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to think on this."

sentences.zh: 行軍司鎧文水武士擭、前太子左勳衛唐憲、憲弟儉皆勸淵舉兵。

translations.literal: Wushi Huo of Wenshui, armorer of the campaigning staff, former Left Merit Guard of the Heir Apparent Tang Xian, and Xian's younger brother Jian—all urged Yuan to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wushi Huo of Wenshui, armorer on the military staff, the former Left Merit Guard attendant Tang Xian, and Xian's younger brother Jian all urged Yuan to take up arms.

sentences.zh: 儉說淵曰：「明公北招戎狄，南收豪傑，以取天下，此湯、武之舉也。」

translations.literal: Jian urged Yuan, saying, "Illustrious lord, recruiting the barbarians of the north and gathering heroes of the south to take the realm—this is an act of Tang and Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Jian told him, "Gather the tribes of the north and the heroes of the south and seize the empire. That would be an act worthy of Tang and Wu."

sentences.zh: 淵曰：「湯、武非所敢擬，在私則圖存，在公則拯亂。

translations.literal: Yuan said, "Tang and Wu are not ones I dare compare myself to; in private I seek preservation, in public I wish to rescue chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said, "I would not dare compare myself to Tang and Wu. For myself I seek survival; for the realm I would put down the chaos.

sentences.zh: 卿姑自重，吾將思之。」

translations.literal: You for now take care of your station; I shall reflect upon it."
translations.idiomatic: For now keep your own counsel. I will consider it."

sentences.zh: 憲，邕之孫也。

translations.literal: Xian was the grandson of Yong.
