translations.idiomatic: Xian was the grandson of Tang Yong.

sentences.zh: 時建成、元吉尚在河東，故淵遷延未發。

translations.literal: At this time Jiancheng and Yuanji were still in Hedong, and therefore Yuan delayed and did not set out.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng and Yuanji were still in Hedong, so Yuan held back.

sentences.zh: 劉文靜謂裴寂曰：「先發制人，後發制於人。

translations.literal: Liu Wenjing said to Pei Ji, "He who strikes first controls others; he who strikes later is controlled by others.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenjing told Pei Ji, "Strike first and you hold the advantage. Strike late and others hold you.

sentences.zh: 何不早勸唐公舉兵，而推遷不已！

translations.literal: Why not early urge Duke of Tang to raise troops, instead of deferring without end!
translations.idiomatic: Why do you not urge Duke Tang to rise now, instead of putting it off again and again?

sentences.zh: 且公為宮監，而以宮人侍客，公死可爾，何誤唐公也！」

translations.literal: Moreover you are palace intendant, yet you presented a palace woman to serve a guest—for your death that might pass, but why mislead Duke of Tang!"
translations.idiomatic: You are keeper of the palace, yet you sent a palace woman to a guest. Your death might be one thing—but why drag Duke Tang into ruin?"

sentences.zh: 寂甚懼，屢趣淵起兵。

translations.literal: Ji was greatly afraid and repeatedly pressed Yuan to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was terrified and repeatedly urged Yuan to take up arms.

sentences.zh: 淵乃使文靜詐為敕書，發太原、西河、雁門、馬邑民年二十已上五十已下悉為兵，期歲暮集涿郡，擊高麗，由是人情恟□，思亂者益眾。

translations.literal: Yuan then had Wenjing forge an edict mobilizing all men of Taiyuan, Xihe, Yanmen, and Mayi from twenty years up to fifty years to become soldiers, with the term set for year's end to assemble at Zhuo Commandery to strike Goguryeo; by this the people's hearts were alarmed and fearful, and those thinking of rebellion grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had Wenjing forge an imperial order calling every man between twenty and fifty from Taiyuan, Xihe, Yanmen, and Mayi to arms, to assemble at Zhuo Commandery by year's end for the campaign against Goguryeo. The people were thrown into alarm and unrest, and those ready to rebel grew ever more numerous.

sentences.zh: 及劉武周據汾陽宮，世民言於淵曰：「大人為留守，而盜賊竊據離宮，不早建大計，禍今至矣！」

translations.literal: When Liu Wuzhou occupied Fenyang Palace, Shimin said to Yuan, "My lord serves as garrison commander, yet bandits have secretly seized the detached palace—if the great plan is not early established, calamity has now arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wuzhou seized Fenyang Palace, Shimin said to Yuan, "You are the garrison commander, yet bandits hold an imperial retreat. Unless we act now, disaster is upon us!"

sentences.zh: 淵乃集將佐謂之曰：「武周據汾陽宮，吾輩不能制，罪當族滅，若之何？」

translations.literal: Yuan then gathered his generals and staff and said to them, "Wuzhou holds Fenyang Palace—we cannot control it; guilt merits clan extermination—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan gathered his commanders and staff. "Wuzhou holds Fenyang Palace and we cannot drive him out. The penalty is extinction of our clans. What are we to do?"

sentences.zh: 王威等皆懼，再拜請計。

translations.literal: Wang Wei and the others were all afraid and bowed twice, requesting a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei and the others were afraid and bowed low, begging for a course of action.

sentences.zh: 淵曰：「朝廷用兵，動止皆稟節度。

translations.literal: Yuan said, "When the court uses troops, every movement and halt must be submitted to the military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said, "In military matters the court decides every move.

sentences.zh: 今賊在數百里內，江都在三千里外，加以道路險要，復有他賊據之；

translations.literal: Now the bandits are within several hundred li, Jiangdu is three thousand li away; add to this roads perilous and narrow, and again other bandits holding them;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels are only a few hundred li away, while Jiangdu lies three thousand li distant. The routes are treacherous and other bandits hold them.

sentences.zh: 以嬰城膠柱之兵，當巨猾豕突之勢，必不全矣。

translations.literal: With walled-in, stiff-instrument soldiers to meet the rush of great rascals like swine breaking loose—complete preservation is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: If we sit behind our walls with a rigid, passive force against a raging enemy, we cannot hold out.

sentences.zh: 進退維谷，何為而可？」

translations.literal: Advance or retreat, both are ravines—what can be done that is acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: We are caught between advance and retreat. What can we do?"

sentences.zh: 威等皆曰：「公地兼親賢，同國休戚，若俟奏報，豈及事機；

translations.literal: Wei and the others all said, "Your lordship's territory joins your kin and worthy men, sharing the state's weal and woe; if we wait for memorial and report, how can we reach the moment of opportunity;
translations.idiomatic: Wei and the others said, "You hold this land and its people. You share the fate of the realm. If we wait for orders from afar we will miss our chance.

sentences.zh: 要在平賊，專之可也。」

translations.literal: What matters is pacifying the bandits—you may take sole authority."
translations.idiomatic: What matters is defeating the bandits. You should act on your own authority."

sentences.zh: 淵陽若不得已而從之者，曰：「然則先當集兵。」

translations.literal: Yuan outwardly as if unwillingly assenting said, "Then we must first gather troops."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan feigned reluctant agreement. "Very well. Then we must first raise an army."

sentences.zh: 乃命世民與劉文靜、長孫順德、劉弘基等各募兵，遠近赴集，旬日間近萬人，仍密遣使召建成、元吉於河東，柴紹於長安。

translations.literal: He then ordered Shimin together with Liu Wenjing, Zhangsun Shunde, Liu Hongji, and others each to recruit soldiers; from near and far they came to assemble, and within ten days nearly ten thousand men; he also secretly sent envoys to summon Jiancheng and Yuanji from Hedong and Chai Shao from Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He put Shimin, Liu Wenjing, Zhangsun Shunde, Liu Hongji, and others in charge of recruitment. Men gathered from far and near, and within ten days nearly ten thousand had assembled. He also sent secret envoys to summon Jiancheng and Yuanji from Hedong and Chai Shao from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 王威、高君雅見兵大集，疑淵有異志，謂武士擭曰：「順德、弘基皆背征三侍，所犯當死，安得將兵！」

translations.literal: Wang Wei and Gao Junya saw troops greatly assembled and suspected Yuan of divergent intent; they said to Wushi Huo, "Shunde and Hongji were all attendants who fled conscription on three occasions—their offense merits death—how can they command troops!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei and Gao Junya saw the great muster and suspected Yuan of ulterior designs. They said to Wushi Huo, "Shunde and Hongji were all attendants who repeatedly deserted the expedition. Their crime is death. How can they lead troops?"

sentences.zh: 欲收按之。

translations.literal: They wished to seize and investigate them.
translations.idiomatic: They meant to arrest and investigate them.

sentences.zh: 士擭曰：「二人皆唐公客，若爾，必大致紛紜。」

translations.literal: Wushi Huo said, "Both men are Duke of Tang's guests; if so, great disorder must surely follow."
translations.idiomatic: Huo said, "Both are Duke Tang's guests. Move against them and you will stir up serious trouble."

sentences.zh: 威等乃止。

translations.literal: Wei and the others thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and the others desisted.

sentences.zh: 留守司兵田德平欲勸威等按募人之狀，士擭曰：「討捕之兵，悉隸唐公，威、君雅但寄坐耳，彼何能為！」

translations.literal: Garrison Adjutant for Soldiers Tian Deping wished to urge Wei and the others to investigate the recruits' dossiers; Wushi Huo said, "The pursuit-and-capture troops all belong to Duke of Tang—Wei and Junya are only seated in delegation; what can they do!"
translations.idiomatic: Tian Deping, adjutant for soldiery on the garrison staff, wanted to urge Wei and the others to examine the recruits' records. Huo said, "The pursuit troops all answer to Duke Tang. Wei and Junya are figureheads. What power do they have?"

sentences.zh: 德平亦止。

translations.literal: Deping also stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Deping gave up the idea as well.

sentences.zh: 晉陽鄉長劉世龍密告淵云：「威、君雅欲因晉祠祈雨，為不利。」

translations.literal: Jinyang district chief Liu Shilong secretly reported to Yuan, saying, "Wei and Junya intend to use the Jinyang shrine rain prayer as an occasion for harm."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shilong, district chief of Jinyang, secretly told Yuan, "Wei and Junya plan to use the rain rites at the Jinyang shrine against you."

sentences.zh: 五月，癸亥夜，淵使世民伏兵於晉陽宮城之外。

translations.literal: Fifth month, night of guihei—Yuan had Shimin hide troops outside the Jinyang palace city walls.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of guihei in the fifth month, Yuan placed Shimin's men in ambush outside the walls of the Jinyang palace compound.

sentences.zh: 甲子旦，淵與威、君雅共坐視事，使劉文靜引開陽府司馬胙城劉政會入立庭中，稱有密狀。

translations.literal: At dawn on jiazi Yuan sat with Wei and Junya jointly handling affairs, and sent Liu Wenjing to lead Liu Zhenghui of Zuocheng, adjutant of Kaiyang Prefecture, to enter and stand in the courtyard, claiming there was a secret report.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on jiazi, Yuan sat in council with Wei and Junya. Liu Wenjing brought in Liu Zhenghui of Zuocheng, adjutant of Kaiyang Prefecture, to stand in the courtyard and announce that a confidential report had arrived.

sentences.zh: 淵目威等取狀視之，政會不與，曰：「所告乃引留守事，唯唐公得視之。」

translations.literal: Yuan signaled Wei and the others to take the report and read it; Zhenghui did not give it, saying, "What is reported concerns affairs of the garrison commander—only Duke of Tang may view it."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan gestured for Wei and the others to read it. Zhenghui refused. "This concerns the garrison commander. Only Duke Tang may see it."

sentences.zh: 淵陽驚曰：「豈有是邪！」

translations.literal: Yuan feigned alarm and said, "How can there be such a thing!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan feigned shock. "Can this be true?"

sentences.zh: 視其狀，乃云：「威、君雅潛引突厥入寇。」

translations.literal: He looked at the report; it said, "Wei and Junya secretly led the Turks in to raid."
translations.idiomatic: He read the report. It said, "Wei and Junya secretly brought in the Turks to raid."

sentences.zh: 君雅攘袂大詬曰：「此乃反者欲殺我耳！」

translations.literal: Junya flung his sleeves and cursed loudly, saying, "This is the rebels wanting to kill me!"
translations.idiomatic: Junya threw back his sleeves and shouted, "The rebels are trying to murder us!"

sentences.zh: 時世民已佈兵塞衢路，文靜因與劉弘基、長孫順德等共執威、君雅繫獄。

translations.literal: At that time Shimin had already deployed troops blocking the thoroughfares; Wenjing thereupon together with Liu Hongji, Zhangsun Shunde, and others seized Wei and Junya and imprisoned them.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shimin's men had blocked the streets. Wenjing, Liu Hongji, Zhangsun Shunde, and the others seized Wei and Junya and clapped them in prison.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，突厥數萬眾寇晉陽，輕騎入外郭北門，出其東門。

translations.literal: On bingyin, several tens of thousands of Turks raided Jinyang; light cavalry entered the outer wall by the north gate and exited by the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the Turks struck Jinyang with tens of thousands of men. Light horsemen rode in through the outer city's north gate and out through the east gate.

sentences.zh: 淵命裴寂等勒兵為備，而悉開諸城門，突厥不能測，莫敢進。

translations.literal: Yuan ordered Pei Ji and others to muster troops in readiness, yet fully opened all city gates; the Turks could not fathom it and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had Pei Ji and the others draw up the troops while throwing every gate wide open. The Turks could not read his intent and did not dare enter.

sentences.zh: 眾以為威、君雅實召之也，淵於是斬威、君雅以徇。

translations.literal: The multitude thought Wei and Junya had actually summoned them; Yuan thereupon executed Wei and Junya as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: The people were convinced Wei and Junya had brought the Turks, and Yuan executed them as a public example.

sentences.zh: 淵部將王康達將千餘人出戰，皆死，城中恟懼。

translations.literal: Yuan's subordinate commander Wang Kangda led a little over a thousand men out to battle—all died; within the city alarm and fear arose.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's officer Wang Kangda rode out with a thousand men and was killed to a man. Panic seized the city.

sentences.zh: 淵夜遣軍潛出城，旦則張旗鳴鼓自他道來，如援軍者；

translations.literal: That night Yuan secretly sent troops out of the city; at dawn they raised banners and beat drums, coming by another route as if relief forces;
translations.idiomatic: That night Yuan sent a detachment out in secret. At dawn they returned by another road with banners flying and drums beating, as though a relief army had arrived.

sentences.zh: 突厥終疑之，留城外二日，大掠而去。

translations.literal: "The Turks in the end remained suspicious; they stayed outside the walls two days, plundered greatly, and departed."
translations.idiomatic: "The Turks remained suspicious, camped outside for two days, plundered heavily, and withdrew."

sentences.zh: 煬帝命監門將軍涇陽寵玉、虎賁郎將霍世舉將關內兵援東都。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang ordered Gate Supervising General Chongyu of Jingyang and Rapid-Tiger Guard Officer Huo Shiju to lead Guanzhong troops to relieve the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang ordered Gate Guard general Chongyu of Jingyang and Rapid-Tiger guard officer Huo Shiju to lead Guanzhong troops to the relief of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 柴孝和說李密曰：「秦地山川之固，秦、漢所憑以成王業者也。

translations.literal: Chai Xiaohe urged Li Mi, saying, "The firm mountains and rivers of Qin territory are what Qin and Han relied upon to accomplish their royal enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Xiaohe urged Li Mi, "The natural fortress of Qin country is what made the Qin and Han thrones possible.

sentences.zh: 今不若使翟司徒守洛口，裴柱國守回洛，明公自簡精銳西襲長安。

translations.literal: Now it would be better to have Grand Steward Zhai hold Luokou, Pillar Duke Pei hold Huiluo, and the Illustrious Lord himself select elite troops to strike west at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Send Grand Steward Zhai to hold Luokou and Pillar Duke Pei to hold Huiluo, while you yourself pick your best troops and strike west toward Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 既克京邑，業固兵強，然後東向以平河、洛，傳檄而天下定矣。

translations.literal: Once the capital region is taken, enterprise is firm and troops strong; then turn east to pacify the He and Luo rivers—proclaim by edict and the realm is settled.
translations.idiomatic: Once the capital falls your position is secure and your armies strong. Then turn east to pacify the Yellow and Luo valleys. Issue your proclamation and the empire is yours.

sentences.zh: 方今隋失其鹿，豪傑競逐，不早為之，必有先我者，悔無及矣！」

translations.literal: Just now Sui has lost its deer and heroes compete in the chase; if not done early, there must be one ahead of us—regret will come too late!"
translations.idiomatic: The Sui has lost the prize and every hero is racing for it. Delay, and someone will beat us to it. Then it will be too late for regret!"

sentences.zh: 密曰：「此誠上策，吾亦思之久矣。

translations.literal: Mi said, "This is truly the superior stratagem; I too have long pondered it.
translations.idiomatic: Mi said, "That is indeed the best plan. I have weighed it myself for a long time.

sentences.zh: 但昏主尚存，從兵猶眾，我所部皆山東人，見洛陽未下，誰肯從我西入！

translations.literal: Only the benighted sovereign still exists, followers and troops are still numerous, all those under my command are men of Shandong—seeing Luoyang not yet taken, who would consent to follow me westward!
translations.idiomatic: But the corrupt emperor still lives and my army is large. My men are all from the east. With Luoyang still untaken, who will follow me west?

sentences.zh: 諸將出於群盜，留之各競雌雄，如此，則大業隳矣。」

translations.literal: The generals came from bandit hosts; keep them and each will compete for supremacy—thus the great enterprise would be ruined."
translations.idiomatic: My commanders rose from the bandits. Leave them idle and each will fight for his own turf. That way the whole enterprise is lost."

sentences.zh: 孝和曰：「然則大軍既未可西上，僕請間行觀釁。」

translations.literal: Xiaohe said, "Then since the great army cannot yet advance west, your servant requests to travel by a secret route and watch for an opening."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohe said, "If the main force cannot march west yet, let me go by a separate route and scout for an opportunity."

sentences.zh: 密許之。

translations.literal: Mi consented.
translations.idiomatic: Mi agreed.

sentences.zh: 孝和與數十騎至陝縣，山賊歸之者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Xiaohe, with several tens of horsemen, reached Shan County; mountain bandits who submitted to him numbered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohe rode into Shan County with a few dozen men, and more than ten thousand mountain bandits rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 時密兵鋒甚銳，每入苑，與隋兵連戰。

translations.literal: At that time Mi's troops' edge was very sharp; each time they entered the park, they fought in succession with Sui troops.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi's army was then at the height of its fighting power, and each foray into the imperial park brought another engagement with Sui forces.

sentences.zh: 會密為流矢所中，臥營中。

translations.literal: It happened that Mi was struck by a stray arrow and lay in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Then Li Mi was hit by a stray arrow and took to his bed in camp.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，越王侗使段達與龐玉等夜出兵，陳於回洛倉西北。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Yue Prince Tong sent Duan Da with Pang Yu and others to sortie troops by night and deploy northwest of Huiluo Granary.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day, Prince Tong of Yue sent Duan Da, Pang Yu, and others out under cover of night and formed battle lines northwest of the Huiluo granary.

sentences.zh: 密與裴會基出戰，達等大破之，殺傷太半，密乃棄回洛，奔洛口。

translations.literal: Mi with Pei Huiji went out to fight; Duan and the rest routed them thoroughly, killing and wounding more than half, and Mi then abandoned Huiluo and fled to Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi and Pei Renji marched out to meet them. Duan Da's force crushed their army, killing or wounding more than half. Mi abandoned the Huiluo position and retreated to Luokou.

sentences.zh: 寵玉、霍世舉軍於偃師，柴孝和之眾聞密退，各散去。

translations.literal: Chongyu and Huo Shiju had their armies at Yanshi; Chai Xiaohe's host, hearing of Mi's retreat, each scattered away.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyu and Huo Shiju were encamped at Yanshi. When Xiaohe's men heard that Mi had pulled back, they broke up and scattered.

sentences.zh: 孝和輕騎歸密，楊德方、鄭德韜皆死。

translations.literal: Xiaohe, with a light horse escort, returned to Mi; Yang Defang and Zheng Detuo both died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohe fled back to Mi with a small cavalry escort. Yang Defang and Zheng Detuo were both killed.

sentences.zh: 密以鄭頲為左司馬，滎陽鄭乾象為右司馬。

translations.literal: Mi made Zheng Ting Left Master of Horse and Zheng Ganxiang of Xingyang Right Master of Horse.
translations.idiomatic: Mi appointed Zheng Ting Left Master of Horse and Zheng Ganxiang of Xingyang Right Master of Horse.

sentences.zh: 李建成、李元吉棄其弟智雲於河東而去，吏執智雲送長安，殺之。

translations.literal: Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji abandoned their younger brother Zhiyun at Hedong and left; clerks seized Zhiyun and sent him to Chang'an, killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji left their younger brother Zhiyun behind at Hedong and fled. Local officials captured Zhiyun, sent him to Chang'an, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 建成、元吉遇柴紹於道，與之偕行。

translations.literal: Jiancheng and Yuanji met Chai Shao on the road and traveled together with him.
translations.idiomatic: On the road Jiancheng and Yuanji met Chai Shao and went on together.
